Writing the tiers as `value`, `midRange`, and `posh` would match the tools.

**Why N3:** The input schema's enum gives the right value, so an agent that reads the schema doesn't do the wrong thing. That makes this unclear text (N3), not false text (F3). It's not D1, since the spelling really is different.

**Note (N2 - A missing test)**

`converse()` has no test, but it holds the logic the task asks for. It reads the trip before each message and takes today's date from the start place with `tripToday()`. It holds each user message until the SDK sends a `result` for the turn before, so the date line goes on the right message. It logs `mirror_error` with the session's ID. The tests cover only the parts: `AppLines`, `tripToday()`, and `coordinatorOptions()`. Here is a break no test would catch. Suppose `converse()` read the start place once, before the loop, instead of before each message. A user who sets the start place on a US evening would then keep the UTC date, a day ahead, for the rest of the session. A test could fake `query` or pull the `userMessages` generator out. It would check that the second message gets the start place's date once a tool has set the start place, and that a `mirror_error` message is logged with the session ID.

**Why N2:** The code looks right, and the pieces it uses are tested, so this is a missing test (N2), not a wrong one (F7). No task item asks for a test of `converse()` itself, so it isn't F1.

title: The coordinator in the terminal

body:
Closes #118

## Do

- Add a test that builds what each agent sees, and compares it to that agent's checked-in file, such as `coordinator.view.md`. The coordinator is the only agent so far. The file has the agent's system prompt, built with the real `settings.json`, then each of its tools: name, description, and input JSON Schema. Get the tools through an MCP client, as the `trip` and `memory` server tests already do, so the file shows them as the SDK gets them. Use Vitest's file snapshot (`toMatchFileSnapshot`), so a file that doesn't match fails the test and prints the lines that differ. A normal test run never writes the file.
- Add `npm run agent-views`, which rewrites the files. It runs only this test with Vitest's `-u`, so it never updates any other snapshot. The check stays in `npm run test`, so `npm run check` and CI fail on a stale file.
- Write both into DEVELOPMENT.md: the command in section 2, and in section 5, that a change to anything an agent reads, or to a setting it shows, comes with its rewritten view file in the same commit. Each issue that adds an agent adds its file to the test.

## Done when

- `coordinator.view.md` is checked in and shows the coordinator's system prompt and every tool it has, with numbers filled in from `settings.json`.
- Changing one tool description, without running `npm run agent-views`, makes `npm run check` fail with the changed line. Running it fixes the failure. Put the failure output in the PR.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Results

- **The view file:** done. `src/agent/coordinator.view.md` has the system prompt and all six tools: `read_trip_brief`, `update_trip_brief`, `read_memory`, `add_memory_item`, `update_memory_item`, and `forget_memory_item`. The numbers 14, 12, 6, 50, and 300 come from `settings.json`.
- **A stale file fails the check:** done. I added " It cannot be undone." to the `forget_memory_item` description and ran `npm run check` without rewriting the view. It failed with this output:

  ```
   FAIL  src/agent/agent-views.test.ts > agent views > matches the coordinator's view file
  Error: Snapshot `agent views > matches the coordinator's view file 1` mismatched

  - Expected
  + Received

  @@ -272,11 +272,11 @@
    ### mcp__memory__forget_memory_item

    Description:

    ````text
  - Removes a memory item for good.
  + Removes a memory item for good. It cannot be undone.
    ````

    Input schema:

    ````json

    Snapshots  1 failed
   Test Files  1 failed | 81 passed (82)
        Tests  1 failed | 610 passed (611)
  ```

  The view file was left as it was. Then `npm run agent-views` rewrote it ("1 updated", 1 test file run), and `npm run check` passed. I put the description back afterward.
- **`npm run check` passes:** done. 82 test files and 611 tests passed.

**Checked by hand:** I deleted the view file and ran the test the way `npm run test` does. It failed instead of writing a new file.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **Where the view file lives:** `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`, next to its test. Prettier skips `*.md`, and the pre-commit hook watches `src/**`, so a commit that changes only the view file still runs the check.
- **`npm run test` now passes `--update=none`.** Without it, a local run would write a missing view file instead of failing, since Vitest writes new snapshots by default outside CI. There are no other snapshot tests, so nothing else changes. DEVELOPMENT.md section 2 says it.
- **`npm run agent-views` passes `--update=all` with the `=`.** Without it, Vitest reads the test file's path as the update mode and runs every test file.
- **The tools come from `coordinatorOptions()`.** The test lists the tools of each server the coordinator is given, so a server added to the coordinator shows up in its view without a change to the test. Tool names are shown as the model sees them, such as `mcp__trip__read_trip_brief`.
- **The coordinator test's fake setup moved to `src/agent/coordinator.fake.ts`,** so both tests share it.
- **The CI fixer may run `npm run agent-views`.** DEVELOPMENT.md now tells it to rewrite the view file when it changes what an agent sees. Joe asked for `"Bash(npm run agent-views)"` to be added to its `--allowedTools` in `.github/workflows/code-review.yml`.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes

None needed.

title: A checked-in file of what each agent sees

body:
Go through what the coordinator sees in `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`, and make the changes agreed along the way. Regenerate the coordinator view after each change.

## Changes

- Drop "so no tool takes a trip ID" from the coordinator's role. The coordinator never sees a trip ID.
- Keep only format and limits in the `update_trip_brief` input descriptions. Drop the examples of what an item means from `focus`, `restDaysText`, `budgetRulesText`, and `mealPreferencesText`. The system prompt already gives them.
- Drop "More than 0" from `comfortableDrivingInHours`, since the schema's `exclusiveMinimum` says it. Keep "at most" the maximum in the description, not as a schema maximum.
- Say user memory carries over from one trip to the next, in place of "The next trip starts from them."

## Results

- `src/agent/coordinator.view.md` is regenerated in each commit, and its diff shows only these changes.
- `npm run check` passes: 82 test files, 611 tests.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **The trip ID clause is gone, and "The trip is set for this conversation" stays.** The coordinator never sees a trip ID, so the clause only explained what the schemas already show. The rest of the line still tells it that it can't switch to another trip.
- **The input descriptions say only how to pass a value.** When a meaning example is in both the prompt and the schema, the two drift apart. They already had: the schema dropped "somewhere warm with good hiking", and the meal example wasn't in the prompt. Format examples stay, such as "8:00 a.m." The reason is in the comment in `src/tools/trip-brief-input.schema.ts`.
- **The maximum stays out of the schema.** A schema failure comes back to the model as a raw validation error, such as `MCP error -32602: Input validation error: ... "Too big: expected number to be <=12"`. A refusal from `TripBriefService` reads plainly. `tripLengthInDays` keeps "from 1 to", since the schema says only more than 0.
- **"Two memories" stays.** Each is its own store, and the memory tools pick one by name.

## Set aside

- An evaluation of how an agent judges budget tiers at the edges between them: in #53's open questions.
- What each budget tier means: in #60's open questions.

## Config changes

None needed.

title: Changes from going through the coordinator's view

body:
Closes #52

## Do

- Add the endpoints: list the user's trips, with name, dates, and last updated; start a trip from the "New trip" form; list a trip's sessions; send a message, with the reply streamed back over Server-Sent Events; and resume a session.
- Check that the signed-in user owns the trip before making a session's MCP servers (tool design, section 4).
- Keep a turn running when the browser disconnects.
- Refuse to start or resume a session, or take a message, once the trip has started. Check before each message.
- Add the home screen: the user's trips, and "New trip."
- Add the trip page: its sessions, with date and title, each with resume, plus "start a new session." Add the chat view, showing the reply as it streams in.

## Done when

- Tests with a fake in place of the Agent SDK (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5) show that another user's trip is refused.
- A stream closed partway through a turn still leaves the whole turn in the transcript.
- A started trip refuses a new message.
- On the deployed site after the merge (systems design, section 7), Joe signs in, starts a trip, and goes through discovery.
- After a reload, resuming the session restores the conversation.
- A new session on the same trip knows the trip brief and memory.
- The second test user, which Joe added in Supabase for isolation tests, sees none of Joe's trips, and the coordinator knows none of his preferences (functional spec 11, S8).
- Closing the tab partway through a reply, then coming back, shows the finished reply.

## Results

- **Another user's trip is refused:** passes. `src/api/chat-isolation.test.ts`. The other user's trip list is empty, and every trip and session route gives a 404. No turn runs.
- **A stream closed partway keeps the whole turn:** passes. `src/api/chat-turns.test.ts` cancels the stream after the first part, and the session then shows the whole reply.
- **A started trip refuses a new message:** passes. `src/api/chat-turns.test.ts`. A new message, a new session, and a resume each get a 409, and no turn runs.
- **Signs in, starts a trip, goes through discovery on the deployed site:** for Joe, after the merge.
- **After a reload, resuming restores the conversation:** passes locally in a headless browser. After a reload, the session page showed the whole conversation. Still to check on the deployed site.
- **A new session knows the trip brief and memory:** passes locally against the real Agent SDK. Asked what it knew, the new session listed the trip brief and both trip memory items. Still to check on the deployed site.
- **The second test user sees none of Joe's trips:** passes locally with a second test user, through the API: an empty trip list, and 404s for Joe's trip and session. The coordinator part, and the deployed site, are for Joe after the merge.
- **Closing the tab partway through a reply, then coming back:** passes locally in a headless browser. On return, the page showed "Working…", then the finished reply once the turn ended.

## Checked by hand

Run locally against the local Postgres and the real Agent SDK, with test sign-in tokens in place of Supabase:

- The reply streamed as it came: each tool's event arrived seconds before the text.
- `curl` cut off 3 seconds into a turn. The turn finished, and the session then showed the whole reply.
- After a resume, the stored user message held the date line and the resumed line. The coordinator read the trip brief and memory before answering.
- Through Caddy 2.11 with `encode` on, as in `docker/Caddyfile`, the stream came compressed (zstd) and still arrived event by event. A tool event came 0.8 seconds before the text.
- In the browser: the home screen, the trip page, Resume, sending with Enter, the "New trip" form, and its address changing to the new session's.
- Starting a Claude Code process took about 0.45 seconds over 3 runs.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **One Claude Code process per turn.** Each message starts a process that resumes the session from its stored transcript, and the process ends with the turn. So nothing runs between turns, and a restart needs no special handling. The process takes about half a second to start. Agreed in chat, and written into systems design section 2.
- **The turn runs apart from the request.** `CoordinatorTurns` (`src/agent/coordinator-turns.ts`) starts each turn and keeps its events in a buffer. The HTTP stream only reads them. When the browser goes away, the stream stops and the turn goes on.
- **Opening a session's page counts as a resume.** It calls `POST /api/sessions/:id/resume`, so the next message gets the resumed line (technical spec 5.2). After a restart, the next message gets the date and the resumed line again, since the app's lines are kept in memory.
- **Coming back while a turn is still running.** The page shows "Working…" and asks `GET /api/sessions/:id` every 3 seconds until the turn ends. That call doesn't mark a resume.
- **The reply streams one event per message from the SDK, not word by word.** The browser gets the text, the name of each tool as it's called, and the end of the turn. Tool inputs and replies show only in `npm run chat`.
- **Another user's trip gets the same 404 as a trip that doesn't exist,** so the reply doesn't say it's there.
- **A started trip's session can't be opened either,** for both resume and the 3-second check (functional spec 2).
- **`npm run chat` uses the same turn runner,** so the terminal and the browser run turns the same way. `converse()` is gone.
- **Tests fake the SDK at the turn's events,** such as text and "turn ended", not at the SDK's own messages. Those need dozens of fields each. The fake (`src/agent/run-turn.fake.ts`) saves transcript lines the way the SDK does with eager flushing.
- **New dependency: `@hono/zod-validator` 0.9.1,** which systems design section 4 names for checking request bodies.
- **A small router of our own (`web/src/route.ts`), not a package.** Each page has its own path, so a reload opens the same page.

None of these but the first went into a design doc. They're how the code does what the docs already say.

## Set aside

- **The chat shows the coordinator's Markdown raw,** such as `**Trip brief**`. Written down in #123, in Triage.

## Config changes

None needed.

<!-- fix-loop: summary -->

## Fix loop: deferred, and needs attention

Code updates this comment after each fix round. Resolve a finding's thread once it's handled. A finding in a review body has no thread, so tick its box instead.

**Deferred**

None.

**Needs attention**

None.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)**

`GET /sessions/:sessionId` goes through `openSession()`, which calls `refuseIfChatClosed()`. So once the trip's start date begins, this route returns 409. The browser calls it from `useCheckRunningTurn()` to find out when a turn it didn't see end has finished. That hook ignores every error and just asks again on the next tick. Technical spec 5.2 says a turn already running at midnight on the start date still finishes. Example: the user sends a message at 11:59 PM the night before the start date, closes the tab, and reopens the session after midnight. The resume itself gets 409, so the page shows the error, and the finished reply never appears. Another case: the tab stays open on a page that loaded with `turnRunning: true`. After midnight every poll gets 409 and is ignored, so the page shows "Working…" forever and the send box stays disabled. A fix could skip the chat-closed check on the read-only GET, or have the poll stop on a refusal.

**Why NF2:** It needs the turn to be running right at midnight on the trip's start date while the browser isn't watching the stream, which is timing that has to line up exactly, so it isn't normal use and gets NF2 instead of F2. No D label fits: the design says a running turn finishes at midnight, and doesn't say what a page waiting on that turn should show.

**Fix (F2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, in normal use)**

When a turn fails inside the Agent SDK, the reason is now dropped everywhere. `turnEventsOf()` turns the SDK's `result` message into `{ kind: "ended", succeeded: false }`. That keeps neither the `subtype`, such as `error_during_execution`, nor the `errors` list or the error `result` text. `CoordinatorTurns.#run()` logs only errors that are thrown, so a turn that ends with an error result is never logged on the server. Example: the Claude API returns an error partway through a browser turn. The SDK sends a result with subtype `error_during_execution`. The browser shows "The reply didn't finish.", and the app log says nothing about it. The terminal chat used to print `The turn failed: <subtype>`. Now it prints only "The turn failed." (src/chat.ts:200). The comment on `#run` says a failed turn "is logged", but this kind isn't. Joe can't tell whether the cause was the API, the tools, or the model.

**Why F2:** A turn that fails with an SDK error result is a failure the code is meant to handle, so this is normal use. The app then does something a user would plainly not expect: it drops a reason the terminal chat used to print, and logs nothing on the server. That makes the agent's behavior hard to trace, which CLAUDE.md asks reviewers to report. It isn't F1, because no task item covers it, and no D label fits.

**Fixed** in f4c35c9480d5b5c6ab28807d2ed0004103870e34.

The "ended" `TurnEvent` now has `failure: string | null` in place of `succeeded`. `turnEventsOf()` fills it from the SDK's result: the subtype and its `errors`, or for a "success" with `is_error`, the `result` text, which the SDK's types say holds the API error. `CoordinatorTurns.#run()` logs a failed "ended" event with the session ID and the reason. The terminal chat prints `The turn failed: <reason>` again. The browser still gets only `succeeded`, which `chatEventOf()` now works out as `failure === null`. The test is "logs why a turn failed, and tells the browser it didn't finish" in `src/api/chat-turns.test.ts`. It runs a failing turn through the chat API with `FakeSdk.failure` set, and failed before the fix because nothing was logged. The mapping from the SDK's own result message isn't unit tested, since building one in a test needs snake_case fields that the lint rules allow only in schema files. The type checker covers it.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)**

A message request whose body isn't valid JSON gets a 500 "Something went wrong." instead of a 400, and the app logs a stack trace as if it were a bug. `zValidator` throws Hono's `HTTPException` (status 400, "Malformed JSON in request body"). The new `api.onError` sends every error that isn't one of the four known classes through `statusOf()`, which returns 500. I checked this locally: `POST /api/trips` with body `{bad` and `Content-Type: application/json` returns `500 {"error":"Something went wrong."}` and logs the `HTTPException`. A fix could return `error.getResponse()` for an `HTTPException`, or map it to its own status.

**Why NF2:** The browser always sends valid JSON, so this only happens with a hand-made or broken request, which isn't normal use. That makes it NF2, not F2. It isn't D1, because the local run shows the 500.

title: Chat in the browser

body:
Closes #125

## Do

- Turn on summarized thinking in the coordinator's options (`src/agent/coordinator.ts`), and add a line about it to the technical spec.
- Pass these to the browser, in order, for each turn the tab sends (`src/agent/turn-event.ts`, `src/api/turn-stream.ts`). Each becomes a raw card on the left:
  - The turn's start: the model and the tools it was given.
  - The message the model got, with the app's lines added, such as the date and the resumed line (technical spec 5.2). It goes on the left, since the app wrote those lines, not the user.
  - Each thinking summary, reply text, tool call with its full input, and tool reply with its full text and whether it was an error.
  - Any other system message from the SDK, such as a retry, as its subtype and data.
  - The turn's end: how long it took, the number of model calls, input and output tokens, and why it failed, if it did.
- Show the conversation as cards, and add the "Raw" toggle and the raw cards to the chat view (`web/src/chat-page.tsx`, `web/src/chat-state.ts`).

## Done when

- A test with a fake turn (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5) shows each kind of item above reaching the browser's stream.
- On the deployed site after the merge (systems design, section 7), Joe turns on "Raw", sends a message that makes the coordinator call a tool, and sees on the left, in order: the start, the message with the app's lines, a thinking summary, the tool call with its input, the tool's reply, the reply text, and the end with its time and tokens.
- With "Raw" off, only the user's messages show on the right and the coordinator's replies on the left.
- After a reload, the conversation is restored as cards, with no raw cards.

## Results

- **Each kind of item reaches the browser's stream:** passes. `src/api/chat-turns.test.ts` gives the fake turn a thinking summary, a tool call, a tool reply, and a retry. The stream carries the start, the message with the date line, those four, the reply text, and the end with its time and tokens, in that order. A failed turn's end carries why it failed.
- **Raw on shows each step in order:** passes locally in headless Chrome, against the real Agent SDK. The message made the coordinator call 4 tools. The left side showed the start, the message with the date line, a thinking summary, each tool call with its input, each tool reply in a box, a second thinking summary, the reply, and the end: "10.7 s · 5 model calls · 15,072 input tokens (13,831 from the cache) · 466 output tokens". Still to check on the deployed site.
- **Raw off shows only the user's messages and the replies:** passes locally in the same run: one user card on the right and one reply card on the left. `web/src/chat-state.test.ts` also checks that a reply's parts join into one card, as a reload shows them.
- **After a reload, the conversation is restored with no raw cards:** passes locally in the same run. After a reload with Raw on, the page showed only the user card and the reply card.

## Checked by hand

Run locally against the local Postgres and the real Agent SDK, with test sign-in tokens in place of Supabase:

- `npm run chat` showed real thinking summaries, so `display: "summarized"` works with this SDK and model. A normal turn sent no other system messages.
- In the browser, the "Raw" toggle shows the cards for turns already sent from the tab, and hides them again.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Joe was away while this was built and asked me to decide open points and list them here.

- **With Raw on, each part of a reply is its own card, in its place among the raw cards.** With Raw off, a turn's parts join into one card, as a reload shows them. So the reply text never shows twice. Written in functional spec 10.1, with the rest of the chat view.
- **"Other system messages" means every SDK message of type `system`, except two.** `init` is the start card. `thinking_tokens` is left out, since it comes many times a second while the model thinks. SDK messages of other types, such as `rate_limit_event` or `tool_progress`, aren't sent. This is in a code comment in `src/agent/turn-event.ts`, not a design doc.
- **Input tokens count everything the model read:** uncached input, plus cache writes, plus cache reads. The end card also says how many came from the cache, such as "15,072 input tokens (13,831 from the cache)". Model calls is the SDK's `num_turns`.
- **The message the model got is added by `CoordinatorTurns`, right after the SDK's start event.** Not by the SDK wrapper, so the fake-turn test runs the real code that adds it.
- **Long text is cut at 15 lines or about 1,500 characters, whichever comes first.** Without the character limit, one long line, such as JSON with no line breaks, would still fill the view. The button says "Show all", then "Show less".
- **The stream's events changed.** The `tool` event is now `toolCall`, with the full tool name and input. The browser shortens the name for "Working: …". The `ended` event now carries why the turn failed, its time, and its usage, in place of `succeeded`.
- **The Raw toggle starts off on each page load,** and isn't remembered.
- **The terminal chat prints the new items too:** thinking summaries, system messages, and the tokens on its end line. It skips the message the model got, since the user just typed it.
- **Docs:** functional spec 10.1 (the chat view and the Raw toggle), technical spec 5.4 (new, summarized thinking), and systems design section 4 (the stream carries each step).

## Security

Why a turn failed now reaches the browser, for every user. It's the SDK's error text, such as "error_during_execution: API Error: 529 Overloaded", or the error's text when the Claude Code process fails. I haven't seen it hold a secret, but it could show server details, such as a file path. Your call whether that's fine.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes

None needed.

**Note (N2 - A missing test)**

No test checks that the "message" event carries the app's lines. The new raw-view test sends "Five days." as the trip's second message on the same date. `AppLines.addTo()` adds nothing to that message, so the expected `{ text: "Five days." }` is just the user's own text. The first test checks only the event names. Suppose `CoordinatorTurns.#run()` added `{ kind: "message", text }` with the user's text and not the message built in `#prepare()`. Every test would still pass, even though the raw card would no longer show the date or resumed line. A test that sends the trip's first message, or a message after a resume, and checks the message event's text starts with "Today is ..." would catch that.

**Why N2:** The test checks the real stream for every event kind, but it misses the case the task names: the message with the app's lines added. So the test isn't wrong (F7). It's a missing case, which is N2.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)**

When `runTurn` throws, the catch block adds an "ended" event with `durationMs: 0` and `usage: null`. The raw card's `EndedBody` then shows "0.0 s" for a turn that may have run for a long time before it failed. For example, if the Claude Code process crashes 40 seconds into a turn, the raw view says "Turn failed" with "0.0 s". That makes the turn look like it failed right away. Leaving out the time when it isn't known, or measuring it in `#run`, would show the real length.

**Why NF2:** This is wrong output in the raw view, but only when `runTurn` throws. An SDK failure normally arrives as an error result that carries its real time, so a throw isn't normal use. That rules out F2 and makes it NF2.

title: Show each turn's steps in the browser chat with a Raw toggle

body:
Closes #123

## Do

- Show the coordinator's replies with their formatting when "Raw" is off, both as they stream in and in a resumed session (`web/src/chat-page.tsx`).
- Show the replies as raw Markdown when "Raw" is on.

## Done when

- With "Raw" off, a reply with bold labels and a numbered list shows them formatted, with no raw marks.
- With "Raw" on, the same reply shows its raw Markdown marks.

## Results

- **Raw off shows the reply formatted:** passes locally in headless Chrome, against the real Agent SDK. I asked for a new trip and for a reply with a bold "Trip brief" label and a numbered list. The reply card showed 15 bold spans, an 11-item numbered list, and a bulleted list, with no `**` anywhere in its text. After a reload, which loads the session from the server as a resumed session does, the same card showed the same formatting.
- **Raw on shows the raw Markdown:** passes in the same run. Each reply part showed as written, such as `**Trip brief**` and `1. **Focus:** Austin to Big Bend (saved)`. After the reload, with Raw on, the whole reply showed its marks too.

## Checked by hand

- Rendered a sample reply to HTML with `react-dom/server`: bold, a numbered list, a GitHub-style table, and a link came out as HTML. A `<script>` tag in the text came out as escaped text, and the link got `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.
- `npm run build:web` builds. The front-end bundle grows from about 541 KB to 698 KB. Vite's warning about chunks over 500 KB was already there on main.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Joe was away and asked me to make the decisions and write them down here.

- **The library is `react-markdown`, with `remark-gfm` for GitHub's tables.** The issue named `react-markdown` as the example. It's the usual choice in React, and it doesn't run HTML found in the text, so a reply can't add a script to the page. `remark-gfm` adds tables, strikethrough, and task lists. The coordinator may well answer with a table, such as one row per day, and without the plugin that table would show as pipes. Written into systems design section 4.
- **Links in a reply open in a new tab.** Following a link in the same tab would leave the chat while a turn might still be running. Written into systems design section 4.
- **The user's own messages stay plain text.** The issue is about the coordinator's replies, and the user doesn't write Markdown on purpose.
- **What the user sees with Raw on and off** is written into functional spec 10.1.
- **`@types/react` moved from `devDependencies` to `dependencies`.** `react-markdown` lists it as a required peer. `src/config/dependencies.test.ts` requires every peer of a production dependency to be a production dependency too, since the app image installs only `dependencies`. The cost is one types package in the app image, which nothing there uses.

## Set aside

- On the new trip in the check, the coordinator's reply began with "I need to read brief and memory first." That's the coordinator describing its own steps to the user, and it's about its instructions, not the chat view. Added as an open question to #65, which finishes the coordinator's instructions.

## Config changes

None.

<!-- fix-loop: summary -->

## Fix loop: deferred, and needs attention

Code updates this comment after each fix round. Resolve a finding's thread once it's handled. A finding in a review body has no thread, so tick its box instead.

**Deferred**

None.

**Needs attention**

None.

**Fix (F2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, in normal use)** With "Raw" off, single line breaks in a reply are lost. `ReplyText` renders the reply with `react-markdown`, which keeps a single newline as a soft break inside one `

` (`line1\nline2` renders as `

line1\nline2

`, checked locally with `react-dom/server`). Then `.card.reply.formatted` sets `white-space: normal`, so the browser shows that newline as a space. The coordinator often writes bold labels one per line with no list marks, such as `**Focus:** Austin to Big Bend\n**Length:** 5 days\n**Start:** May 1`. Before this PR, `pre-wrap` showed those as three lines. Now they run together as one paragraph: "Focus: Austin to Big Bend Length: 5 days Start: May 1". A resumed session shows the same thing. One fix is to add the `remark-breaks` plugin, so each single newline becomes a `
`. **Why F2:** This is wrong output in normal use, since one bold label per line is a common way for the model to format a trip brief. The task asks for bold labels to show formatted, and a user would expect them on separate lines as the model wrote them. No design doc says single newlines should be joined, so D2 doesn't fit, and the claim was checked by rendering locally, so D1 doesn't fit.

**Fixed** in 2424eadef2ca0323a6e37b956b464f091c3ca58c. `ReplyText` in `web/src/reply-text.tsx` now runs a small local remark plugin, `remarkLineBreaks`, after `remark-gfm`. It splits each text node on its line endings and puts a `break` node between the lines, so each one renders as a `
`. This is the same thing `remark-breaks` does. I wrote it in the file because the sandbox couldn't reach the npm registry to add that package. Code blocks and inline code keep their text, since they hold a value and have no text nodes. A Markdown hard break still renders once. I checked that by rendering, and tables were unchanged too. The new test `web/src/reply-text.test.tsx` renders `ReplyText` with `react-dom/server`. It checks bold labels one per line, a list item with a second line, and a code block. The first two failed before the fix and pass now. I also added a sentence to systems design section 4 saying each line the coordinator ends shows as a new line.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)** `NewTabLink` turns every link into a new-tab link and drops every prop except `href`, `title`, and `children`. That breaks the footnotes that `remark-gfm` makes. I rendered `Hi [^1]\n\n[^1]: note` locally. The footnote mark came out as `1`, and the back link as `↩`. Clicking the mark opens the app again in a new tab instead of scrolling to the note. The back link has no target to go to either, because the `id` on the mark was dropped. The footnote section also shows a visible "Footnotes" heading, because nothing in `app.css` defines the `sr-only` class. One fix is to set `target="_blank"` only when `href` doesn't start with `#`, and to pass the other props through. **Why NF2:** The app does the wrong thing, but only when the coordinator writes a Markdown footnote. That's an input the model has little reason to produce in a chat reply, so it's outside normal use. That rules out F2, and NF2 fits. The claim was checked by rendering locally, so D1 doesn't fit, and no design doc speaks to footnotes or in-page links, so D2 doesn't either.

**Not fixed:** below the bar.
It only goes wrong when the coordinator writes a Markdown footnote, which it has little reason to do in a chat reply. Joe can still ask for it.

title: Show the coordinator's Markdown formatted in the chat

body:
Closes #54

## Do

- Add `find_place` and `read_place` on the `places` server, and give them to the coordinator. `read_place` checks the place belongs to the session's trip.
- Add `read_itinerary`, for the whole trip or scoped to a day, stay, or stop. Leave out route lines.
- Add the itinerary to the resume line and to the coordinator's instructions on reading at the start of a session, and the bullet on open warnings, as open question 3 says.
- Measure a full read of a 14-day trip: its characters, and its tokens as the API counts them.
- Make `read_itinerary` return an error when its reply would be over 25,000 tokens, such as "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return." The tool can't count tokens without calling the API, so it checks the reply's characters. Set that limit from the measured characters per token, with room to spare, so the tool stops before Claude Code's limit would.

## Done when

- In a chat with the coordinator, it resolves "Moab," and answers "is Milt's open on Mondays?" from `read_place`. Milt's is a stop on Moab Day 2, in the example trip in domain model section 5.2.
- Tests on the example trips (domain model, section 5) show what each scope returns.
- The measured size, the 25,000-token limit, and the error are written into tool design section 2.1. If the 14-day trip's full read is near the limit, Joe hears about it before #55 starts.
- A test shows a read over the limit returns the error.

## Results

**The chat.** Run with `npm run chat` against the local database, on a trip seeded like the Moab example: Moab for 3 nights, Torrey for 1, and Day 2's six stops, all real Google places, with legs routed by Google. The coordinator first read the trip brief, the whole itinerary, and memory.

```
> Hi! Before we go further, can you look up Moab for me and make sure it's the one in Utah?
  [tool] mcp__places__find_place {"text":"Moab","where":"Utah"}
  [reply] Matches for "Moab, Utah", best first:
          - Moab (place_f3ggdztx). Type: none. Address: Moab, UT 84532, USA.

Yes, it's the right Moab. Google lists it as **Moab, UT 84532, USA**, and it's the same place your trip's first stay already uses.
```

```
> Great. Is Milt's open on Mondays?
  [tool] mcp__places__read_place {"placeId":"place_bvynvyzp"}
  [reply] Milt's Stop & Eat (place_bvynvyzp)
          ...
          Opening hours:
          - Monday: 11:00 AM – 8:00 PM
          ...

Yes. Google lists Milt's Stop & Eat as open Mondays from **11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.** Your lunch there is planned for 12:00 to 1:00 p.m. on Monday, October 11, which fits well within those hours.

Google's hours are for a normal week, and that Monday is Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples' Day. Small places sometimes change their hours on holidays or close for the season, so check with Milt's closer to the trip.
```

It took the place ID for Milt's from its whole read of the itinerary. In its first reply it also mentioned the open warnings: "Still open from last time: opening hours aren't confirmed for Delicate Arch Trail, The Windows Section, or Corona Arch Trailhead."

**Tests of each scope** are in `src/tools/itinerary-tools.test.ts`, on the two example trips:

- Moab Day 2, line for line: its leg, its schedule in time order with the times domain model 5.2 gives, each stop with its candidates, and its check results.
- The Torrey stay: its lodging, Day 4 with its drive hours approval, and stargazing at 1:00 a.m. the next day.
- The Milt's stop, line for line.
- The whole Moab trip: its ends and dates, each stay and its days in order, the last day, and all 14 check results.
- The Monterey stay, with the breakfast near it on Day 2, which belongs to the San Luis Obispo stay.
- San Francisco's last day, with its route type approval.

`src/tools/itinerary-read-marks.test.ts` covers candidates in two sets with their full details, results new and already known, an approval that no longer applies, weather text out of date, rejected places, a new trip with nothing set, and bad scopes.

**The size, written into tool design 2.1.** The trip measured is a 14-day loop with 8 stays, five stops a day, and 312 candidates (`src/domain/fourteen-day-example.fake.ts`). Its whole read is 72,264 characters. The API counts it as 38,271 tokens for `claude-opus-5-5`, which is 1.89 characters a token. Plain English came to 2.9. The limit is 40,000 characters, about 21,000 tokens at that rate.

**The 14-day trip's full read is over the limit, not just near it.** It's about 38,000 tokens against Claude Code's 25,000. So `read_itinerary` refuses it, and the coordinator reads a long trip a stay or a day at a time. At that density a whole read fits a trip of about a week. #129 is a spike to work out how to handle it.

**The test over the limit.** "refuses a whole read of a 14-day trip as too large, and still reads its days", in `src/tools/itinerary-read-marks.test.ts`. The reply is the error "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return. Read one day, stay, or stop at a time instead."

## Checked by hand

- **Token counts.** Measured by sending the text to `claude-opus-5-5` through the Agent SDK, and taking the input tokens less those of a one-word prompt. The plan token has no API key for the count endpoint.
- **Resume.** Resuming the chat session, the coordinator read the trip brief, the whole itinerary, and memory before it answered "What's on Day 2 again?".
- **`find_place` against Google.** Seeding the trip ran 12 real lookups through `PlacesClient`, saved with `PlaceWriter`. In the chat, `find_place` gave back Moab's existing place ID.
- **Permissions.** The coordinator's tool list in the chat had `find_place` and `read_place`, named one by one in `allowedTools`, and both ran.
- `npm run check` passes: 91 test files, 660 tests.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Joe asked me to make the decisions this work needed and list them here. Each one below is a proposal: approving the PR agrees to it.

Settled in the issue, and built that way:

- **The size limit** is 25,000 tokens (open question 1). The measured size, the limit, and the error are in tool design 2.1.
- **The read makes its own calendar and checker** (open question 2), as `look_up_stay_weather` does. `TripSession` now has `settings` and `now` in place of `limits`. `TripReader` is unchanged.
- **The resume line and the reading instructions** use open question 3's wording. The open warnings bullet adds "whether they're marked new or already known", from technical spec 5.2. Without it, the bullet would clash with "Stay quiet about check results marked already known" in the Check results section.

Made while building, and written into tool design 2.1:

- **The scope is required.** The coordinator passes "all" for the whole trip, or an ID. Tool design 2.1 said "optional scope", but our rule is no optional inputs, so a whole read is asked for by name.
- **Days, stops, and sets are counted from 1,** as the UI and the user count them. Stored set numbers start at 0.
- **What each read gives for a candidate.** A whole read or a day gives each candidate's set, place, short line, and visit and detour times, plus the selected one's rationale. A stay or a stop also gives every candidate's rationale, tier, how it was found with its link, and notes. Tool design 2.1 only said the rationale comes with a scoped read. I put the other three there too, to keep whole reads small.
- **A read doesn't show results that went away.** Nothing is saved, so the next write's reply reports them as gone.
- **A read doesn't show a leg's routed places, best order, or time saved.** They're only there to tell when to route the leg again. The stop order note gives the best order when it matters.
- **The limit is 40,000 characters.** At the measured 1.89 characters a token, that's about 21,000 tokens, so there's room for text with more IDs. The error also says what to do: "Read one day, stay, or stop at a time instead."

Made while building, and written into tool design 2.3:

- **`find_place` returns up to 5 matches,** best first. When Google finds nothing, the reply says so, and it isn't an error.
- **`read_place` leaves out Google's place ID and the opening periods.** The periods say the same as Google's hours lines, which it does show.

Made while building, and written into domain model 3.10:

- **The short line leaves out a town that's just the place's own name.** In the chat, the read showed "Delicate Arch Trail, 5.0 stars, Delicate Arch Trail". Its address, "Delicate Arch Trail, Utah, USA", has no town. A town such as Grand Junction also showed as "Grand Junction (…), Grand Junction". `src/domain/place.test.ts` has a test that fails without the fix.

Made while building, and not written into a design doc:

- **The coordinator's tools on the `places` server are named one by one** in `allowedTools`, such as `mcp__places__find_place`. That server will also hold `search_near` and `search_along_leg`, which only workers get (tool design 3).
- **The `read_itinerary` description** tells the coordinator to read only the part a question is about, and that a whole read of a long trip can come back as an error.
- **A failed Google Places call is now an error the agent can read,** like the other Google calls.
- **`find_place` loads the trip on every call,** to mark rejected places. That's one extra read per lookup.
- **The 14-day trip** is `src/domain/fourteen-day-example.fake.ts`, next to the other example trips. Its places are made up, but each has the length of a real name, type, and address.

## Set aside

- **Whole reads of long trips.** A 14-day trip's whole read is about 38,000 tokens, so the tool refuses it. Technical spec 5.2 has the coordinator read the whole itinerary at the start of a session, after a resume, and for "what's left to decide?". How to handle that is #129, a spike.
- **Offering to rerun the weather worker** when a forecast becomes available waits for #64, as open question 3 says.

## Config changes

None needed.

<!-- fix-loop: summary -->

## Fix loop: deferred, and needs attention

Code updates this comment after each fix round. Resolve a finding's thread once it's handled. A finding in a review body has no thread, so tick its box instead.

**Deferred**

- Once a whole read is refused, the design leaves some of the trip unreachable through any scope (`design/tools.md:32`): [finding](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/pull/128#discussion_r4364853766), [reply](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/pull/128#discussion_r4364873306), #55

**Needs attention**

None.

Line 32.

**Fix (F6 - A design doc is wrong, so an agent building from it would build the wrong thing)**

Once a whole read is refused, the design leaves some of the trip unreachable through any scope. First, the trip length check result has the itinerary's ID as its subject (`tripLengthResult` in `src/domain/stay-checks.ts`). `checkLines` in `src/tools/itinerary-lines.ts` shows it only in a whole read, since each day, stay, and stop scope filters results by subject. Second, a stay's lodging, lodging candidates, and weather text appear only in a whole read or a read of that stay. A day read leaves them out (`dayScopeLines`). Concrete case: on a 10-day trip where the brief asks for 11 days, `read_itinerary` with "all" returns the too-large error. Then no scoped read shows "The trip is 10 days, and the brief asks for 11." The new SESSION_START bullet tells the coordinator to mention open warnings in its first reply, so it misses this one. Second case: section 2.1 says a stay of 5 nights or more at the measured density is refused too. For such a stay, its weather text and its lodging candidates' rationales can't be read at all, since a day read never includes them. Neither the doc nor the open question in #55 says how the coordinator reaches these items. Both of #55's proposed answers (a slimmer whole read, or reading a stay at a time) would still leave the long-stay case open, and the second would also leave the trip-level results open.

**Why F6:** The code does what tool design 2.1 says, but that design gives wrong behavior in normal use: a trip over about a week, or a stay of 5 nights or more, is a trip a real user plans. D2 doesn't fit because #55 has an open question on long-trip reads. D3 doesn't fit because no code comment hands this work to #55, and #55's question doesn't name the unreachable trip-level results or the long stay's lodging and weather.

**Deferred:** #55.

The claim holds. `checkLines` shows results whose subject is the itinerary, such as `tripLengthResult`, only in a whole read. The start and end places, the dates, and the rejected places are also only in a whole read. `dayScopeLines` leaves out the stay's lodging and weather text, and a stay of 5 nights or more is refused too. Nothing breaks yet, though. No coordinator tool can add a stay until #55 adds `add_stay`, so no trip today is large enough to be refused. The fix also depends on how #55 settles its open question on reading a long trip, which is settled in chat with Joe. A slimmer whole read would cover the trip-level parts, and the long stay needs its own answer. I added both cases to that open question, naming this PR and finding, and noted that neither proposed answer covers them all. The fix to tool design 2.1 and to the read's scopes belongs with that answer, so this round changes no code or docs.

title: Read the itinerary

body:
Closes #55

## Do

- Add these tools and `compute_route`. Each write's reply is built from what the write hands back, as tool design section 2.1 says.
- Report check results whose text changed. Today a result that's still there after a write is "already known", so the reply leaves it out unless the write touched its subject, even when its text changed. Example: the user lowers their driving hours from 6 to 5, and Day 2's warning now gives the new limit, but the reply doesn't show it. Make `FeasibilityChecker.compare()` mark a known result whose text differs from its saved match as "changed". Each write's reply lists changed results anywhere in the trip, like new ones. The coordinator decides whether to raise one. Write it into domain model 4.8 and tool design 2.1. Then take out `touchedBy()` in `src/tools/trip-brief-tools.ts`, which PR #44 added for the driving hours only. Raised in PR #44's third review.
- Add the coordinator's instructions for anchors and stretches, the shape and skeleton rounds, broken feasibility rules, and changes to stays.

## Done when

In a chat with the coordinator:

- The coordinator sets up the Moab trip from domain model section 5.2: start and end places, start date, Moab for 3 nights, Torrey for 1, and the Dewey Bridge waypoint. A read shows each leg's drive time.
- Asked for Seattle to Miami in five days at four hours a day, it says how far short the plan falls and offers trade-offs (functional spec 11, S3).

## Results

Both chats ran with `npm run chat`, against the local database and real Google, on 2026-10-24, each for a new dev user.

- **Moab: done.** From one message giving the trip, the coordinator looked up each town and Dewey Bridge with `find_place`, then called `update_itinerary` (Grand Junction, Salt Lake City, October 10, 2027), `add_stay` for Moab (3 nights, midRange, "stays of 2+ nights") and Torrey (1 night, value, "the default tier"), and `set_waypoints` on Day 1 with the Dewey Suspension Bridge. Each reply gave the legs' new road time, such as "Day 1: 1 h 44 m → 2 h 12 m, 110 miles." The whole read then showed every leg: Day 1 110 miles, 2 h 12 m of road time; Day 4 156.2 miles, 2 h 37 m; Day 5 213.1 miles, 3 h 18 m. It checked with `compute_route` that Moab to Torrey already passes through Capitol Reef. It held back the trip length warning while the stays were going in.
- **Seattle to Miami: done.** `compute_route` gave 48 h 12 m and 3,297 miles. The coordinator said: "Five days at 4 hours a day only covers 20 hours, about a third of the way." It offered three trade-offs: 5 days at about 10½ hours a day, 14 days at about 3¾ hours, or about 9 days at 6 hours. Then it compared a central and a southern route for March weather.

## Checked by hand

- `compute_route` against real Google: plain names such as "Sacramento, CA" came back with their match, such as "Sacramento, at Sacramento, CA, USA."
- Google Routes with Atlanta as a pass-through point on Seattle to Miami returns `{}`. With Atlanta as a stop, it returns a route. The other five cities in that call each work as pass-through points.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Joe agreed to the first one in chat. He asked me to make the rest and write them down here, for review in this PR.

**`compute_route` matches plain names with Google Places.** Google Routes never says what a plain name matched, so the tool runs a Text Search for the best match first. It asks only for the ID, name, and address, which makes it a Pro call, not a rated one. It then routes by the match's place ID, and the reply gives each match's name and address. Nothing is saved. Written into tool design 2.4, and Google design 2.1, 2.4, and 5. Recorded as a struck-out open question in #55.

**A route can take a place that isn't saved.** `RoutePath` and `StopsPath` now take a `RoutablePlace`: a Google place ID, plus a name and address for errors. That way `compute_route` can route a match it didn't save. A leg still routes the trip's places. Code only, in `src/domain/route-finder.ts`.

**Each segment's distance comes back from Google.** Tool design 2.4 says `compute_route` gives the distance from each stop to the next. So the Routes field list adds `routes.legs.distanceMeters`, a basic field that doesn't change the price. A leg still keeps only its total. Written into Google design 2.3.

**The no-route error names the pass-through points, and says to try one as a stop.** In the Seattle to Miami chat, two `compute_route` calls with six pass-through points failed with "Google found no driving route from Seattle to Miami." I checked against Google: Atlanta as a pass-through point gives `{}`, and Atlanta as a stop works. Written into tool design 2.4 and Google design 2.4.

**"Changed" is a fourth list in the check comparison.** `compare()` returns `changedResults`: results that aren't new, but whose text differs from the saved match. Every write's reply lists them anywhere in the trip, as "Changed warning: …". A read doesn't mark them. It already gives each result's current text, so a changed one shows as already known. Written into domain model 4.8, tool design 2.1, and persistence design 8.2. Technical spec section 8 said the opposite: a driving warning that got worse stayed already known, and the coordinator stayed quiet. I replaced that with the new rule, and added the "changed" sentence to the broken feasibility rules bullet in technical spec 5.2. `touchedBy()` is gone. A brief change now touches only the itinerary.

**Every itinerary write lists the stops on days that now start or end somewhere else.** Tool design 2.1 named `add_stay` and a moved stay. A new start place, end place, or stay town changes a day's ends too, so every write to the itinerary lists them. Those days count as touched. Written into tool design 2.1.

**Smaller tool rules,** all written into tool design 2.1:

- An update tool refuses a call that changes nothing, as `update_trip_brief` does.
- `update_day` applies its inputs in this order: rest day, start time, the approval to remove, then the approvals to set.
- `set_waypoints` refuses a place given twice.

**What the coordinator's instructions cover now.** These are new: the planning rounds (anchors and stretches, discovery, shape, and skeleton), a stay's tier and rule, days and approvals, changes to stays, the full check results section as settled in #55, and the two memory changes as settled. Some parts of technical spec 5.2 need tools that come later, so I left them out for now:

- Must-sees that are one place, and the fill. #56 and #60 already cover these.
- "Reject the hotel if it no longer fits…" and the Monterey example. These are now in #56's Do list, word for word.
- "Then send workers for any lodging or stop whose candidates no longer fit." This is now in #60's Do list, word for word.

**The tier example changed after the first chat.** At first, the prompt's example was "mid-range, from the rule: 2+ nights". The coordinator copied that whole phrase into `tierRule`, so the read said `from the rule "mid-range, from the rule: 2+ nights"`. The example now gives the tier and the rule apart. A second run saved "stays of 2+ nights" and "the default tier".

**The prompt test ignores "February 14".** The test that catches setting numbers written into the text forbids 14. The memory example agreed in #55 has the date "February 14", which isn't a setting.

## Set aside

- The "changed" mark may come back too often. A daily driving warning's text names its day, so adding a stay before that day renumbers it, and the warning comes back changed. Added to #65's open questions.

## Config changes

None needed.

<!-- fix-loop: summary -->

## Fix loop: deferred, and needs attention

Code updates this comment after each fix round. Resolve a finding's thread once it's handled. A finding in a review body has no thread, so tick its box instead.

**Deferred**

None.

**Needs attention**

None.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)**

`endsOf()` decides whether a day now starts or ends somewhere else by comparing `calendar.fromPlaceOf()` and `calendar.toPlaceOf()`. Both give the stay's `sleepsAt`, which is the selected lodging once there is one, not the stay's town. Tool design 2.1 says a new stay town changes where a day starts or ends, so the reply should list that day's stops. Case: the Monterey stay has a selected hotel, and `update_stay` moves it to Bakersfield. `sleepsAt` is still the Monterey hotel, so no day is listed, and the coordinator doesn't get the stops it's told to go through with the user. The reverse also happens. A later write that selects a hotel changes `sleepsAt` but not the town. That write would list the stay's neighbouring days as "now runs Moab", though nothing moved. `locationOf()` uses the town (`stay.place`), so comparing the stays' places would match what the line says.

**Why NF2:** The reply leaves out the moved days, which is wrong behavior. But it happens only once a stay has selected lodging, and no tool in this PR or before it can select lodging, so it's not normal use yet. It isn't D1, since the code does behave this way.

Fixed in 7f409e4. A day's ends are now compared by the stays' towns, as the "now runs" line gives them. Tests cover both cases: a stay moved to a new town with its hotel unchanged, and a hotel selected with the town unchanged.

**Fix (F7 - A test is wrong)**

The test "marks a day that stays put as a rest day, which removes its leg" checks only that the reply starts with "Changed Day 3 (day_…)." `updateDay()` writes that line no matter what it changed. So if `update_day` ignored `isRestDay`, or `DaysService.setRestDay()` stopped removing the leg, this test would still pass. For example, delete the `setRestDay(...)` call in `updateDay()`, and the test stays green. It should read the day back, or check the reply's leg change, and check that Day 3 is a rest day with no leg.

**Why F7:** The test targets marking a rest day and removing its leg, but it can't catch a break in either one, so it's a wrong test (F7), not a missing one (N2). The labels above it don't fit: the claim is true, and the code under test isn't shown to be wrong.

**Fixed** in e512aeb7b3e8a3d8b82d6a221d693bae7599aedd.

The test was weaker than the finding said. In moabExample(), Day 3 is already a rest day, so the call changed nothing. The test "marks a day that stays put as a rest day, which removes its leg" in src/tools/day-tools.test.ts now first sets isRestDay to false, and checks that a read of Day 3 has no "Rest day." Then it marks Day 3 as a rest day. It checks that the reply lists "Day 3 (…): 1 h → no leg.", and that a read gives "Rest day." and "- No leg." I changed updateDay() for a moment to skip setRestDay() when isRestDay is true, and the test failed. Then I undid that change.

**Fix (F7 - A test is wrong)**

The test "approves longer driving on Day 1, which makes its warning approved" checks only that the reply starts with "Changed Day 1 (day_…)." That line is the same whether or not an approval was saved. So if `updateDay()` skipped `services.days.approveDriveHours()`, or saved the wrong hours, the test would still pass. It should check that Day 1's driving warning comes back marked approved, or that a read of Day 1 shows the 4.5-hour approval with its reason.

**Why F7:** The test names the approval and the approved warning as what it checks, but it asserts neither of them, so it can't catch a break in what it targets (F7). It isn't D1, since the assertion really is only the unconditional "Changed" line.

**Fixed** in e512aeb7b3e8a3d8b82d6a221d693bae7599aedd.

Day 1 of the Moab example drives 2 h 12 m, under the 4 comfortable hours, so it has no driving warning to mark approved. So the test now checks the approval itself, and I renamed it "approves longer driving on Day 1, and a read gives the approval". It checks that a read of Day 1 has no approval before the call. After the call, it checks that the read gives '- Approval: drive hours, up to 4.5 hours of driving, because "a slow day on the river". It applies.' I changed updateDay() for a moment to skip services.days.approveDriveHours(), and the test failed. Then I undid that change.

title: Build the skeleton

body:
## Task

Make sure the UI supports the following:

- Delete trips.
- Able to see user and trip memories when you have a trip chat open, and the ability to delete any of them.
- Able to download the trip brief and itinerary while you have a trip chat open. This would be in a "prettified" JSON format so it's easy for a user to read, that is, multi-line and indented.

These are direct API calls from the UI, not agent tools.

## Done when

- **Delete trips:** the trip page has "Delete trip", which asks first, then goes to the home screen. `DELETE /api/trips/:tripId` removes the trip's row, sessions, transcript lines, places, and trip memory. Tests in `src/api/trip-manage.test.ts` pass.
- **See and forget memory in the chat view:** a "Memory" toggle in the chat view lists user memory and trip memory, each item with "Forget", which asks first. Tests in `src/api/memory-routes.test.ts` pass.
- **Download the trip brief and itinerary:** the chat view has "Download plan" (readable, with place names) and "Download plan as stored" (place IDs, plus the places they link to). Both are indented JSON. Tests in `src/api/plan-downloads.test.ts` and `src/api/trip-manage.test.ts` pass.
- `npm run check` passes: 708 tests.

## Checked by hand

Against the local Postgres, through the real API routes with a test sign-in token:

- The memory list showed one user item and one trip item. Forgetting the trip item returned 204, and the list then showed only the user item.
- The stored download held the linked start place and left out a place the plan doesn't link to. The readable one showed the start place as `{"name": "Start town", "address": ...}`.
- Before the delete, the trip had 1 trip row, 1 session, 2 transcript lines (the coordinator's and a worker's), 2 places, and 1 trip memory item. After `DELETE`, all were 0, the user memory item was still there, and the trip page returned 404.
- With another connection holding the trip's row lock, `deleteTrip()` waited 5 seconds, then refused with the busy error. Once the lock was let go, the delete went through.
- `npm run build` builds the front end. The UI itself wasn't checked in a browser, since that needs a real Supabase sign-in.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Joe chose the first three in chat. The rest I decided.

- **Both download forms.** "Download plan" is readable: each place's name and address where the plan has its ID, and no route lines, which are encoded map lines. "Download plan as stored" is the plan document as stored, followed by every place it links to, with all the place's stored facts. Places from searches that the plan doesn't link to are left out. Written into functional spec 10.1.
- **The coordinator is told when the user forgets memory in the list.** The next message gets an app line: "The user forgot memory items in the app, outside this chat. Read memory again, and stop using any item that's gone." Without it, the coordinator could keep using an item from an earlier `read_memory`. Its instructions list the line, so `coordinator.view.md` changed. Written into technical spec 5.2.
- **Design doc changes merge after the CI review,** without a separate sign-off on the text.
- **The memory routes go by the session,** `/api/sessions/:sessionId/memory`, like the memory tools. So the line goes to that session only. Another session open at the same time doesn't get it, the same as with trip changes, which functional spec 10.1 already doesn't support. Written into technical spec 5.2 and persistence 8.8.
- **The memory list and forgetting refuse a closed chat,** like resuming does. A started trip's chat can't be opened anyway, and its trip memory can't change.
- **A trip can be deleted at any time, even once it has started,** but not while one of its sessions has a turn running (409). The running turn would go on changing the trip. Deleting isn't a write: it takes the row lock "for update," with the same 5-second wait, and doesn't check the started-trip lock. Written into persistence section 6 and 8.2.
- **One repository call removes every table's rows,** `TripRepository.remove()`, so deleting stays one call in one transaction. Written into persistence 8.7.
- **"Delete trip" is on the trip page only,** not the home screen. The downloads are in the chat view only, as asked. The trip page could also get them, so a started trip's plan can still be downloaded, if you want that.
- **Empty links keep their ID name in the readable download,** such as `"selectedPlaceId": null`, since code can't tell an empty place link from an empty stay link by name alone.
- **The button says "Forget"**, the word the functional spec and the agent use.
- **A trip the coordinator is busy with returns 409, not 500.** `TripBusyError` wasn't mapped before. Only the delete can raise it from a route.

## Set aside

- A real-agent test that the coordinator obeys the new line goes into #69's open questions (memory tests), once this merges.

## Config changes

None.

**Note (N6 - A design doc is unclear, or doesn't match the code, in a way no builder would act on)**

The new bullet "When the user forgets memory items in the chat view's memory list" sits between the "When a session is resumed" bullet and that bullet's three sub-bullets. Those are "A restart loses what a cut-off worker said", "Already known may mean another session heard it", and "Two sessions of one trip open at once aren't supported". So in the Markdown they now nest under the memory bullet. They're about resuming and restarts, not about forgetting memory. The new bullet should go after the three sub-bullets, so they stay under the resume bullet.

**Why N6:** The doc's structure is wrong, but each sub-bullet's text still makes clear it's about restarts and resumes, so no builder would build the wrong thing. That makes it N6, not F6. It isn't false (D1) or handed to another issue (D3).
**Fixed** in ec297c6.

Line 416.

**Note (N6 - A design doc is unclear, or doesn't match the code, in a way no builder would act on)**

Section 8.6 still says "Places are never removed." Domain model section 6 says the same: "A place is never removed, even when it's rejected." But this PR's `TripRepository.remove()` runs `DELETE FROM places WHERE trip_id = $1` when a trip is deleted. The PR's own text in section 6 and the `remove(tripId)` entry in 8.7 also say the trip's places are removed. The "never removed" lines need "except when their trip is deleted", as the PR did for transcript lines in section 6.

**Why N6:** The docs contradict each other. But sections 6 and 8.7 say plainly that deleting a trip removes its places, so no builder would act on the old line. That makes it N6, not F6. The claim is true, so D1 doesn't fit.
**Fixed** in ec297c6.

title: Delete trips, see and forget memory in the chat view, and download the plan

body:
Closes #132

## Task

### Do

Joe isn't available while this runs, so don't stop to wait for answers. When a choice comes up, make it, and list it in the PR's decisions comment. When something can't be made to work, write down what was tried and what failed, then go on to the next item.

Answer each of these with working code, and write the answers into `research/agent-evaluations.md`. Lay it out like `research/agent-sdk-tool-scoping.md`: a note that it's research, not design, then Method, then Results.

- **Run Phoenix locally** as a Docker Compose profile in `compose.yaml`, listening only on `127.0.0.1`, with no sign-in. Use an exact image version. Say where its data is kept: its own volume, or a database in our Postgres.
- **Trace a coordinator turn** on the Agent SDK version the app uses (0.3.301). Add `@arizeai/phoenix-otel` and `@arizeai/openinference-instrumentation-claude-agent-sdk`, at exact versions. The SDK must be imported through the instrumented module, or no traces are made, so `runTurnWithSdk` in `src/agent/coordinator.ts` needs to change. Say whether each MCP tool call shows up with its inputs and result, and whether token counts do.
- **Run one evaluation case from start to finish** with `@arizeai/phoenix-client`: a dataset, a task, and scorers, run as an experiment. The task sends scripted user messages to the coordinator through the same code as `npm run chat` (`src/chat.ts`), for a new trip. Use a fresh user UUID each run, so memory starts empty. Set up any memory beforehand through the memory code (persistence design section 8.8), not SQL. Use the "user or trip memory" check from #48: "we never eat at chains" goes to user memory, and "skip I-35 this time" goes to trip memory.
- **Score it two ways.** One scorer is code that reads what was saved from the database. One is a model judge on `claude-haiku-5-5`, called with the Anthropic SDK and paid for with the Max plan's API credits. Its key is in `.env` as `JUDGE_API_KEY`. The name must not start with `ANTHROPIC_`. An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` would make the coordinator bill API credits instead of the plan (`src/agent/claude-env.ts`). Check that the coordinator still runs on the plan token. The key is short-lived. If it's missing, or a call fails because it expired, write that down and go on without the judge. If the judge can't run on the Anthropic API for another reason, write down why. Don't switch to another provider, such as OpenRouter. Joe decides that, since he'd need credits there.
- **Run the case five times.** Say how much the results change from run to run. Using the token counts in the SDK's result message for each turn, and the judge's API usage, say how much one run takes.

Push the spike code to `spike/phoenix-evals`, a branch that never gets a PR, so merging the doc doesn't delete it. The doc links to it. The code doesn't need to pass `npm run check`.

### Done when

- `research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it.
- On the spike branch, one command runs the case and the experiment shows up in Phoenix.

## Results

- **`research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it.** Section 2.1 covers Phoenix in Compose, 2.2 tracing a turn, 2.3 one case from start to finish, 2.4 the judge's key and the plan token, and 2.5 and 2.6 the five runs and what one run takes.
- **On the spike branch, one command runs the case and the experiment shows up in Phoenix.** On [`spike/phoenix-evals`](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/tree/spike/phoenix-evals), `npm run eval:memory -- --repetitions 5` ran 5 of 5 tasks and 10 of 10 evaluations, and printed the experiment's link, `http://127.0.0.1:6006/datasets/RGF0YXNldDox/compare?experimentId=RXhwZXJpbWVudDoy`. Phoenix's REST API returned the experiment with `successful_run_count: 5`.

Checked by hand: Phoenix listens only on `127.0.0.1:6006` (`ss -ltn`), and a refused tool call's span is marked as an error. On the spike branch, the app's 708 tests pass with the instrumented SDK.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Each is written into `research/agent-evaluations.md`. This PR settles them: approving it agrees to them.

1. **Phoenix keeps its data in its own volume, `phoenix-data`, as SQLite, not in our Postgres** (section 2.1). Traces aren't app data. In their own volume they stay out of the app's database and its nightly backup, and removing the volume removes them all.
2. **The image is `arizephoenix/phoenix:20.26.0`,** the standard one, not the `-nonroot` one. Phoenix runs only on this machine, so the nonroot image's file permission setup on the volume wasn't worth trying.
3. **Only port 6006 is published,** on `127.0.0.1`. It carries the UI, the REST API, and traces over HTTP. The gRPC trace port, 4317, isn't needed.
4. **The instrumented SDK gets a tracer that looks up the global provider for each span** (`GlobalTracer` in `src/agent/claude-agent-sdk.ts` on the spike branch, section 2.2). Set up as Phoenix's docs show, it made no spans, because `register()` replaces the global provider object.
5. **Phoenix's address is in code,** `PHOENIX_URL` in `src/tracing.ts`, not in an environment variable. It's always the local container.
6. **One user memory item is added before the conversation,** "Usually drives up to 6 hours a day.", through `MemoryWriter.add()`. That shows the setup path the issue asks for. Both scorers leave it out.
7. **The judge doesn't grade which memory each statement went to.** The code scorer does that. The judge grades three things code can't: faithful, told, and nothing-extra (section 2.3). It answers each with passed or failed, and code works out the score.
8. **A judge call that can't run returns no score and a label that says why,** instead of failing the run. The code score still counts.
9. **The plan check starts one Claude Code process with the coordinator's environment,** sends "Reply with the word OK.", and reads `apiKeySource` and `accountInfo()` (section 2.4). The patched `query()` has no `accountInfo()`, so it uses the SDK's own `query()`.
10. **Runs go one at a time** (`concurrency: 1`), so each one's tokens and time can be told apart.
11. **I added `npm run eval:rejudge`, which wasn't asked for.** It runs only the judge again on an experiment's saved conversations. The judge failed four of five runs that the code scorer passed, and this was the way to tell its spread from the coordinator's (section 2.5).
12. **The spike branch's commits skip the pre-commit hook,** since the issue says its code doesn't need to pass `npm run check`. Four lint errors are left there.
13. **Each turn's span is ours, `coordinator.turn`, with the instrumentation's span under it** (section 2.2). Its input is the message the model got, with the app's lines, and its `session.id` is the agent session ID.
14. **The turn's tokens go on one LLM span, `coordinator.model_calls`, under the turn span.** Phoenix counts tokens only on LLM spans. The SDK gives only the turn's totals, so the one span stands for all of the turn's model calls.
15. **The turn span leaves out the SDK's cost.** On a resumed session it's the session's total so far, not the turn's. For the same reason, a run's SDK cost in the eval summary is now its highest, not the sum. That halved the doc's figures, from $0.19 to $0.21 a run to $0.085 to $0.095.

## Set aside

These are now open questions in #53:

- whether the coordinator may add a note for itself to a memory item, which the judge graded both ways
- functional spec 10.2 giving "no chain restaurants" as a trip memory example, while #48 expects "we never eat at chains" in user memory
- getting the user's message and the right token counts into each turn's trace
- installing `@arizeai/phoenix-client` for good, without `--legacy-peer-deps`

**One for you to decide:** the `GlobalTracer` problem looks like a bug in `@arizeai/openinference-instrumentation-claude-agent-sdk`, or in how it works with `phoenix-otel`. Reporting it upstream would post to Arize's public repo, so I haven't. Say if you want me to.

## Config changes

None.

body:
## Task

Update `research/agent-evaluations.md` with what the spike found after #133. The spike branch replaced Phoenix's Agent SDK instrumentation with spans from our own code. Each turn now has a span for each model call, holding its thinking, text, tool calls, and tokens, in order with a span for each tool call. Only the research doc merges into `main`. The code stays on `spike/phoenix-evals`.

### Done when

- The doc describes the model call spans, with the output that shows them.
- The doc's earlier findings about the instrumentation stay, marked as the first try.

## Results

- **The doc describes the model call spans, with the output that shows them.** Section 2.2 opens with "Spans from our own code": a turn's trace from `npm run chat`, what each kind of span holds, and where the tokens come from. Two chat turns' model calls added up to the terminal's counts (46,944 and 1,476, then 26,644 and 371), and Phoenix's session total was their sum. Section 2.3 has an experiment run's trace, with Phoenix's 102,941 tokens matching the app's count. Section 3 is updated to match.
- **The doc's earlier findings about the instrumentation stay, marked as the first try.** They're in 2.2 under "First try: Phoenix's instrumentation".

nodes.body:
## Decisions

1. **The turn's spans are made from the SDK's messages, and the instrumentation is gone from the spike branch** (section 2.2). Our spans show what the instrumentation left out, and putting the model call spans in one list with the tool spans meant making the tool spans too.
2. **The coordinator's options turn on the SDK's stream events** (`includePartialMessages`) on the spike branch. Without them, each model call's output tokens are the count from when it started. `turnEventsOf()` leaves the events out, so the chats don't change.
3. **A model call span has no input.** What it got is the turn's message or the tool results before it, which are already on other spans.
4. **The thinking is recorded twice on a model call span:** as an OpenInference `reasoning` content, and in `output.value` as JSON. I couldn't see how Phoenix's UI draws a `reasoning` content, so the JSON makes sure it's readable either way.
5. **The eval summary no longer prints the SDK's cost.** It came from the instrumentation's spans. Phoenix shows each run's price.

## Set aside

- **Whether workers' model calls can be traced the same way** went into section 3 as an input for #53. I've updated #53's open question about the turn's trace to point to it.

## Decisions

Each one is proposed here. Approving the PR agrees to them.

- **The coordinator's instructions weren't changed.** It started the worker from a message alone, so the line about the worker that the issue allowed wasn't needed.
- **Workers run in the foreground on the spike branch.** With two workers, the coordinator left out `run_in_background`, and the `Agent` tool ran both in the background. The turn ended before they did. So the spike sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` in the Claude Code process's environment, and both workers then ran at once, inside one turn. Whether a worker may run in the background stays #60's open question. I added this finding to it.
- **A worker's model call spans come from its transcript, and its tool spans from the stream.** The SDK sends none of a worker's stream events, so the stream never has a call's final tokens. The transcript has the tokens, the thinking, and the text, but only once the turn is over. Its tool calls and results do come through the stream, as they happen. So `forwardSubagentText` stays off.
- **A worker's span starts when the coordinator's `Agent` call arrives,** not at the SDK's `task_started` message. The worker's first model call was written to its transcript a few milliseconds before `task_started` arrived, so its span started before its parent's.
- **Span names follow the worker's type:** `coffee-finder.turn` and `coffee-finder.model_call`, with `agent.name` on the worker's span. This matches `coordinator.turn` and `coordinator.model_call`.
- **The telemetry log receiver wasn't built.** Claude Code's `api_request` events have each call's exact tokens. I checked them with a throwaway listener in one turn only. The doc lists it as an option for exact worker output counts.
- **The spike branch's coordinator test now expects `Agent`** in the coordinator's tools, so its 708 tests still pass, as section 1 says. The branch also has `npm run spike:subagent`, which prints `getSubagentMessages()` for one worker.

- **Phoenix's price is still lower than the SDK's.** For the turn in section 2.7, Phoenix gave $0.054 and the SDK $0.062. Section 2.6 already notes the gap, and this spike didn't look into it either. Part of it here is the worker call whose output count was low, and part is the session title call, which has no span.

Bring it as #136 leaves it, so a worker's spans go under the coordinator's `Agent` tool span once workers exist (#60, #61, #64). No worker exists yet, so tests use a fake worker's messages. Besides the spike's `session.id`, each turn's span gets the user's ID as `user.id`, so a trace shows whose chat it is.
