## Do

Build the spike in `scratch/worker-spike/`. `scratch/` is gitignored, so the code never reaches the repo, and it doesn't need to pass `npm run check`. What the next session needs goes in the research doc.

When a choice comes up, make it, and list it in the PR's decisions comment. When something can't be made to work, write down what was tried and what failed, then go on to the next item.

- **Set up a small TypeScript project** with `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` pinned to exactly 0.3.301, the app's version. Sign in to Claude the same way the app does. Give it a coordinator with a short system prompt, on the app's coordinator model (`claude-opus-5-5`), and one worker, on `claude-haiku-5-5`. Give the worker a few fake in-process tools that keep their state in memory: a read of its brief's facts, an add tool that takes a stop ID and one to three items, and `report_result`. No trip data, Postgres, or Google.
- **The result pattern.** Add the `SubagentStop` hook and the `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent`, as in the pattern above. Show:
  - that a worker that tries to finish without calling `report_result` is sent back, and then calls it.
  - the output shape `updatedToolOutput` needs for `Agent`, and that the coordinator sees only the replaced result.
  - how code ties each worker's tool calls to its own `Agent` call, so it can build that worker's result. Check this with two workers running at once.
- **Workers in the foreground.** With two workers sent in one turn, find the setting that keeps both in the foreground, so the coordinator's turn waits for both, and the SDK starts no second turn on its own. Try the definition's `background: false`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` in the Claude Code process's environment. Say whether the two still run at the same time.
- **Each worker's own tools.** Give the worker its own in-process MCP server through its definition's `mcpServers`. Show which tools the coordinator sees, and that it can't call the worker's. Show that the worker doesn't see the coordinator's own tools, or only the ones its `tools` list names.
- **Only our own workers.** Make the `Agent` tool offer only our worker. The SDK docs name `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` for the built-in agents, and an `Agent(fork)` deny rule for forks. Show what the tool's description lists, and what happens when the coordinator is asked to start `general-purpose`, `Explore`, `Plan`, `claude`, or `fork`.
- **Resume after a cut-off worker.** Give the spike a `sessionStore` that writes each line to a file, so a resume takes the same path as the app's `TranscriptAdapter` (persistence design section 6). Stop the process while a worker is running, after it has called a tool. Then resume the session with a new message. Say whether the resume works, and what the coordinator sees for the unfinished `Agent` call. If it doesn't work, try leaving the unfinished lines out of what the store hands back, and say which lines those are.
- **Write the answers into `research/agent-evaluations.md`,** as a new section under Results, after section 2.7. Give each answer with the output that shows it, and a short code example of the pattern that works, with the hooks and the agent definition. Then say, for each of #60's open questions above, what the spike found, so #60 can settle it.

## Done when

- `research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it, and a code example of the working pattern.

Closes #182

## Results

- **`research/agent-evaluations.md` answers each Do item, with the output that shows it, and a code example of the working pattern.** Done, in the new section 2.8:
  - The result pattern: "The result goes through a tool", with the send-back, the `updatedToolOutput` shape, and how code ties each worker's calls to its `Agent` call, checked with two workers at once.
  - Workers in the foreground: a table of the three settings tried.
  - Each worker's own tools: a table of five ways to place the worker's server, and one of the worker's `tools` list.
  - Only our own workers: a table of the five agent types, with and without `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1`.
  - Resume after a cut-off worker: the stored lines, and what the coordinator saw on resume.
  - "The pattern that works": the agent definition, the coordinator's options, the hooks, and the worker's HTTP server.
  - "What this means for #60": one item for each of #60's open questions on the worker.

Checked by hand: every result in section 2.8 comes from a run of the spike in `scratch/worker-spike/`, against the real models on the plan's token. The tool lists come from a local proxy that logged each Messages API request.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **The worker's tools ended up on an HTTP MCP server in the spike's own process.** The task asked for in-process tools. An in-process server can't go in an agent definition, and one in the query's `mcpServers` is the coordinator's too (research section 2.8, "Each worker's own tools"). The tools still run in our process and keep their state in memory. Only the transport changed.
- **The spike logged each Messages API request through a local proxy,** set with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. It logged request bodies only, never headers. So the tool lists in section 2.8 are what each model was sent, not what a model said it had.
- **The `SubagentStop` hook got a limit of two sends back, and checks the agent type.** Without them, it sent a `general-purpose` agent back nine times (section 2.8, "The result goes through a tool").
- **The spike didn't try leaving the unfinished lines out on resume,** since the resume worked with every line. The task said to try it only if it didn't.
- **The `Agent(fork)` deny rule wasn't tried on its own,** since `fork` was refused as "not found" without it.

## Proposed answers

These are what the spike found for each of #60's open questions on the worker. #60 settles each one.

- **The worker brief and result:** the pattern in #182 works on 0.3.301. It needs `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1`, an `Agent` hook that returns the whole output object with its `content` replaced, and a `SubagentStop` hook with a limit that checks the agent type.
- **Resuming after a cut-off worker:** the SDK resumes as is, and tells the coordinator the `Agent` call's outcome is unknown. The transcript adapter needs no change.
- **Background workers:** no. A background worker's own free text reaches the coordinator in a task notification, so it skips the result pattern. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` keeps every worker in the foreground, and two still run at the same time.
- **How workers get their place searches:** on an HTTP MCP server named in each worker's definition. That's the only way the spike found to keep a worker's tools out of the coordinator's tool list. The other choice is an in-process server the coordinator also sees, with a `PreToolUse` hook that refuses its calls.
- **Only our own workers:** `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1`. No `Agent(fork)` rule is needed.

## Security

- **The spike's HTTP server took any request on its port, on 127.0.0.1.** In the app, any process that can reach that port could call the worker's tools. Section 2.8 suggests a key made for each turn, in the URL or a header. #60 decides.

## Set aside

- **Claude Code adds an `# Environment` block to the coordinator's context,** after the user's first message. It has the working folder, the OS, rules about downloaded files, and the agent-type list. The view files don't show it. Opened #188 in Triage.

## Config changes

None.

Technical spec 6.5 is new, and covers how a worker is started, the hooks and settings, and the result. nodes.body:
## Decisions

#191 was moved from chat to the PR on 2026-10-27, at Joe's request. These are the proposed answers. Approving the PR agrees to them.

### The design in short

The coordinator starts a worker with the `Agent` tool. The worker reads the facts for its stops and stay with `read_worker_brief_facts`, adds candidates with the candidate tools, and ends by calling `report_result` with its problems and questions. Hooks record those calls, and replace the worker's last message with a result that code builds. So no free text from a worker reaches the coordinator.

Each agent, the coordinator included, runs from a definition that lists every tool it gets. All the tools stay on our in-process servers, built for each turn with the trip, as today.

### Each decision

1. **The coordinator runs as a named agent, and worker tools stay in-process.** Written into technical spec 2 and 6.5, and tool design 1, 3, and 4.
   - With `agent: "coordinator"`, the session's main agent runs from a definition. Its `tools` list sets what it's sent. It's still the same agent, with the same transcript and system prompt.
   - Today the coordinator gets every tool in the session. With this change, the query's options only say what tools exist, and each definition picks its own.
   - So `search_near` and `search_along_leg` go on the `places` server, and the coordinator isn't sent them. In the spike, the coordinator was told to call a worker tool, and said it "isn't one of the tools I have."
   - This replaces the HTTP listener with a key for each turn. That setup works too, and the key reached the server on every request. But it adds a listener, a key store, and a second way to build servers. The other choice, a `PreToolUse` hook that refuses the coordinator's calls, still shows the coordinator every worker tool.
   - Systems design section 2 doesn't change.

2. **Workers get `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` from the session.** Written into tool design 1. A worker can't get a built-in tool the session doesn't have. So the query's `tools` is `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch`, and only the worker definitions list the web tools.

3. **The coordinator's `Agent` entry names the worker types,** as `Agent(stay-researcher, leg-scout, weather-worker)`. Written into technical spec 6.5. Each agent's type is in the table in technical spec 1. The coordinator's own definition is also an agent type. With plain `Agent`, the coordinator could start a copy of itself.

4. **The worker brief is split between the prompt and `read_worker_brief_facts`.** Written into technical spec 5.3, and tool design 2.1.
   - `read_worker_brief_facts` is on the `trip` server. It takes the worker brief's stop and stay IDs as a list.
   - For a stay, it returns the stay's town with its place ID, dates, nights, activities, and lodging candidates already offered.
   - For a stop, it returns the stop's day with its ID and date, its kind, purpose, set time, and search area, the day's other stops in order, and the candidates already offered.
   - The coordinator writes only what takes judgment: the IDs, roughly when each stop falls, the user's words that apply, interests and must-sees, what memory says to avoid, and the request for "More options", "Higher tier", or "Lower tier".
   - The prompt follows a fixed outline with a heading for each item. #60 drafts the wording.
   - Technical spec 5.2 changes too. The coordinator no longer reads a stop or stay before sending a worker for "More options", since the worker reads the candidates already offered itself.
   - The weather worker gets `read_worker_brief_facts` too, so its worker brief holds only stay IDs. The coordinator has those from its start-of-session read and the "Weather out of date" notes, so it never reads the itinerary just for this worker. The stay's activities move from `look_up_stay_weather` to this tool.
   - The reply is the same for every worker, even where a worker doesn't use part of it, such as lodging candidates for the weather worker. That keeps the tool from depending on who calls it. It changes only if evaluations show the extra facts confuse a worker.

5. **`report_result` is on a new `worker` server.** Written into tool design 1, 2.6, and 3.
   - It takes problems and questions for the user, each a required list that can be empty.
   - It returns "Result recorded. You're done." A second call replaces the first.
   - All three workers get it, so the weather worker's result follows the same pattern.
   - It doesn't fit the `trip` server's job, since it doesn't touch the trip.

6. **The result's lines** are written into technical spec 6.5. In order, they are:
   - each candidate tool's or `set_stay_weather`'s reply, as the tool gave it
   - "No candidates added for:", followed by the worker brief's stops and stay that got none. For the weather worker, "No weather saved for:" and its stays with no saved text
   - the problems and the questions, or "none"
   - If a worker was sent back twice and still didn't report, a line says so instead. #60 drafts the exact wording.

7. **The items already settled in PR #189 are written in as they were.** That's the three hooks, the two environment settings, every definition listing its tools, and the resume. Written into technical spec 6.5, and persistence design 7.

8. **View files** are written into DEVELOPMENT.md section 5.
   - A built-in tool, such as `Agent` or `WebSearch`, is listed by name only, since Claude Code writes its text.
   - The coordinator's view also lists each worker type's description and tools. That's the list the coordinator is told about, so it's text the model reads.

### Set aside

- **#193 (Triage):** `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` each make their own model call, and it runs on the session's model, Opus, even from a Haiku worker. That uses the plan's limits at Opus's rate. Nobody has looked yet for a setting that changes it.
- **Not checked:** whether `Agent(stay-researcher, leg-scout, weather-worker)` alone also hides the SDK's built-in agent types. The design keeps `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` as settled, so it doesn't matter.

### Config changes

None.

## Checked by hand

The init line listed the same 24 tools and `claude-opus-5-5`. The coordinator called `read_trip_brief`, `read_itinerary`, `read_memory`, and `find_place` for Denver, Moab, and Grand Junction. Then it called `update_itinerary` (start place, end place, start date), `add_stay` twice, and `update_trip_brief`. Each reply was a success, and no check results came back. Then I asked it to read the itinerary back. It called `read_itinerary` with scope `all`, which returned the 3 days and both stays, and it summed them up correctly.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Joe asked me to decide these on my own for this issue, though it says "Settled in: chat".

- **The definition's `model` is set to the coordinator model setting, the same as the query's `model`.** The SDK's docs for `agent` say a named main agent runs on its definition's model. A definition with no model can get a default subagent model instead. Setting both the same means it doesn't matter which one the SDK uses, the same reason the prompt is set in both places. Written into technical spec 6.5.
- **The definition lives in its own file, `src/agent/coordinator-definition.ts`,** with the tool names as a list per server, built from the server name constants. It keeps `coordinatorOptions()` short, and the worker definitions in #198 and #60 can sit beside it in the same way. No design doc change.
- **The definition's `description` is "Talks to the user and plans the trip. It's the session's main agent, so it's never started as a worker."** The SDK requires one. No model reads it today. Once the coordinator's `Agent` entry names only the worker types (technical spec 6.5), the coordinator isn't told about its own type either. No design doc change.
- **`allowedTools` is left as it was.** The issue's test compares the definition to it, and changing permissions belongs with the worker tools that need them. I added the question of what it should list to #198's open questions. No design doc change.
- **The view test lists a built-in tool by name only, and fails on an MCP tool name that no server has.** DEVELOPMENT.md section 5 already says built-in tools are listed by name only. The failure means a typo in the definition shows up in `npm run check` instead of silently dropping a tool from the view. No built-in tool is listed today, so that part isn't exercised yet. No design doc change.

## Set aside

- What `allowedTools` should list once workers exist. Written down in #198's open questions.

## Config changes

- None needed.

**Note (N5 - A code comment is wrong)**

The comment above `coordinatorDefinition()` says the main agent gets "the query's model". The same PR's new line in technical spec 6.5 says the opposite: the SDK runs a named main agent on its definition's model. Someone reading only this comment could think the definition's `model` is unused and remove it. Then the main agent could fall back to a default subagent model.

**Why N5:** Only a code comment is wrong, and the code and the design doc next to it are right. It isn't F6, because the design doc is correct.

**Note (N2 - A missing test)**

The test says the definition lists each tool `allowedTools` lets the coordinator use, but it never reads `allowedTools` or the servers' tools. It checks `definition.tools` against a hand-copied list. `allowedTools` allows whole servers (`mcp__trip`, `mcp__memory`, `mcp__routing`). So if a new tool is added to the trip server and left out of `COORDINATOR_TOOLS`, both lists still match and the test passes. The coordinator would be allowed to use the tool but never be sent it. The test would catch that case if it listed each server's tools, filtered them through `allowedTools`, and compared the result with the definition.

**Why N2:** The test still fails if a tool is dropped from today's list, so it isn't wrong (F7). It misses the case where a server gains a tool, which makes it a missing test.

Closes #199

## Results

- **`read_worker_brief_facts`:** `src/tools/worker-brief-facts-tool.test.ts` reads the Moab trip as planned. For a stay, it checks the town with its place ID, the nights and dates, the lodging candidates already offered, and the activities, including Panorama Point at 1 a.m. on the next date, and the stops along the Torrey day's leg. For stops, it checks the day's ID, number, and date, each stop's kind, purpose, search area, and set time ("none" when it has none), its candidates already offered, and the day's stops in order with their times and selected places. It also checks that two stops on one day share one day's part, and that a stop with nothing offered says so. It errors for a check-in, a day ID, and a stop ID the trip doesn't have.
- **Candidate tools:** `src/tools/candidate-tools.test.ts` saves a lodging set to the Moab stay, a meal set to the Gifford stop along Day 4's leg, with detour times worked out against the leg, and an attraction set near the Torrey stay, with visit times and no detour. Each reply is the set's line, then one line per candidate, and the read shows the new set. It also checks the refusals: a candidate shape that doesn't fit the stop's kind, a place already a candidate, a place given twice, a rejected place, a check-in, and a link that isn't https or http. Each refusal saves nothing, and a repeat is refused before any route is asked for.
- **`look_up_stay_weather`:** `src/tools/weather-tools.test.ts` checks the whole reply, which now ends with the weather lines.
- **Left out of the coordinator's definition:** a test in `src/tools/trip-server.test.ts` checks that the coordinator's definition doesn't list the three tools. `src/agent/coordinator.view.md` is unchanged.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

The issue says "Settled in: chat", but Joe asked for these to be decided without him this time. Each one is here for review.

1. **Notes are a required string, "" when there are none.** Code saves "" as no notes. A tool has no optional inputs (tool design section 4), and an empty string is the plainest "none" for free text. Written into tool design 2.1.
2. **The source link must start with https:// or http://.** The option card links to it, and the link can come from a web page the worker read. A `javascript:` link there could run a script in the user's browser. The error says which links are taken. Written into tool design 2.1.
3. **Each candidate in `add_stop_candidates` is one of two shapes: one with a tier, one with `visitTimeInMinutes`.** Every field in each shape is required. The tool refuses a shape that doesn't fit the stop, and the error says what the stop's kind takes, such as `Day 4, Stop 2 (stop_…), meal: "pie" is a meal stop, so each candidate takes a tier, and no visitTimeInMinutes.` I weighed two other ways. Optional `tier` and `visitTimeInMinutes` would go against "no optional inputs". A `kind` field on each candidate would make the worker pass something code already knows. A candidate with both fields fails the schema. The SDK's error then names the extra key in each shape, which is readable. Written into tool design 2.1.
4. **The candidate tools check the places before they work out any detour time.** A place already a candidate there, a place given twice, or a rejected place refuses the call before any call to Google. A worker asked for "more options" can easily offer an old candidate again, and those Google calls would be wasted. For a rejected place, the error gives the user's reason. The domain still refuses all of these too. Written into tool design 2.1.
5. **What each line of a candidate tool's reply gives.** The first line names the set and the stop or stay as `find_in_trip` names them, such as `Set 2 for Day 4, Stop 2 (stop_…), meal: "pie": 2 candidates.` or `Lodging set 1 for Stay 2, Torrey (stay_…): 3 candidates.` Each candidate line gives the place's name, ID, and short line, its visit and detour times, its rationale, its tier, and its notes. It leaves out how the place was found and the link. Code passes these lines to the coordinator in the worker's result, and a whole read lists no candidates. So the lines are all the coordinator has to talk about the options without a read. The order is the read's: Why, then Tier, then Notes. Written into tool design 2.1, with an example.
6. **How `read_worker_brief_facts` lays out its reply.** Each stay, and each day with stops asked for, is one part, in the order the IDs were given. Stops on the same day share their day's part, and an ID given twice counts once. The reason is size: a Moab stay researcher can be sent six stops on Day 2. One part per stop would list that day's six stops six times. A day's part has three pieces. First comes the read's day line. Then each stop asked for, with its kind, purpose, search area, and set time (always given, as "none" when it has none), and under it the candidates already offered. Each offered candidate shows as its set, its place line, and whether it's selected, with no rationale. Last come all the day's stops, each as a whole read gives its line. A stay's part is the read's stay line, then its lodging candidates already offered, then its activities. Written into tool design 2.1, with an example.
7. **The input is named `stopOrStayIds`,** to match `stopOrStayId` in `select_candidate` and `select_user_place`. Not in a design doc, since it's a field name.
8. **The activities kept the weather tool's wording,** moved as they were, such as `- a hike, no place picked yet: Monday, October 11, 2027, 1:15 p.m.` Not in a design doc.
9. **`read_worker_brief_facts`' description says "Call it first, with every stop and stay ID the worker brief gives, in one call."** Tool design 2.1 says the tool is called first. That's about this one tool, so it goes in its description. #60 can still decide whether the stay researcher's instructions say it too. Not in a design doc, since it's wording.
10. **A check-in gets the same error from all three tools:** `stop_… is a check-in. A check-in has no candidates, so no worker fills it.` The coordinator's error for a check-in tells it to select the hotel for the stay. That doesn't fit a worker. Written into tool design 2.1.
11. **A worker's name for a place is filled in without a word in the reply.** `select_user_place` says when it kept Google's name instead. A worker always passes a name and has nothing to do about it (tool design 2.1), so the line would only add noise. Not in a design doc. Tool design 2.1 already says the name is used only when Google has none.
12. **A worker write's reply is only what the change did.** It gives no leg changes and no check results. Adding candidates doesn't change any selected place, so no leg changes for the worker to report. Not in a design doc. Tool design 2.1 already says these writes return no check results.

## Set aside

- **What the stay researcher's instructions say about each candidate field.** This covers `howFound`, `sourceLink`, the rationale, `notes`, and `visitTimeInMinutes`. The input descriptions give only the format (tool design section 4), so the meaning goes in the instructions. Added to #60's open questions.

## Noticed

- The Moab example (`src/domain/moab-example.fake.ts`) routes Day 1's leg before it sets the Dewey Bridge waypoint. So every write in a test re-routes Day 1 at the finish. It only affects tests. The candidate tests count the routes through the candidates' places, not every route.

## Config changes

None needed.

**Note (N3 - Text a road trip agent reads is unclear, or says something twice, or is an error message with the wrong reason for a failure)**

READ_WORKER_BRIEF_FACTS_DESCRIPTION says "Each place shows as its name, place ID, and a short line of facts." But the stay's activities don't follow that. activityName() in activity-lines.ts gives only placeText(place) and the ID, such as "Delicate Arch trail (place_…): Monday, October 11, 2027, 6:00 a.m. to 8:40 a.m.", with no short line. A weather worker that expects a town or type for each activity's place won't find it. It would have to call look_up_stay_weather or find_place to learn where a far-off activity is.

**Why N3:** The description is unclear about one kind of place. An agent that believes it isn't led into a wrong action, since the place ID it needs is there, so this is N3, not F3. The design (tool design 2.1) doesn't say activities get the short line, so D2 doesn't fit.

Line 170.

**Note (N6 - A design doc is unclear, or doesn't match the code, in a way no builder would act on)**

Tool design 2.1 gives two different first lines for the candidate tools' reply. The older paragraph at line 170 gives the example "Set 1 for stop_k7m2x9qa: 3 candidates". The new paragraph at line 182 says the first line names the stop or stay as find_in_trip does, such as 'Set 2 for Day 4, Stop 2 (stop_…), meal: "pie": 2 candidates.' The code (setLines() in candidate-tools.ts) follows line 182. The example at line 170 should match it.

**Why N6:** The doc doesn't agree with itself, but the newer paragraph and its example block say exactly what to build, so no builder would follow the old example. That makes it N6, not F6.

## Decisions

- **Day 1 is routed twice in the Moab example, not routed after the waypoint.** A waypoint needs the day's leg, and the leg exists only once the day is routed. So the example routes Day 1, sets the waypoint, and routes it again, as `LegsService` does after `set_waypoints` in the app. The drive times stay the same, since a waypoint isn't a stop. No design doc change.
- **The candidate tests' route count now checks every route.** Each route has to go through one of the candidates' places, so a test fails if a write routes any other leg. Before, the count skipped other routes, which is how the extra Day 1 route went unnoticed. No design doc change.
- **Tool design 2.1's example activity has no town in its short line.** Google's address for Delicate Arch Trail has no town, so its short line gives only the type and rating. It shows the case #64's new open question is about. Written into tool design 2.1.

## Set aside

- How the weather worker tells that an activity is far from the stay's town, when its short line has no town. Added to #64's open questions.

## Config changes

None needed.

**Note (N5 - A code comment is wrong)**

The comment above `activityLines()` says "The short line's town tells the weather worker whether an activity is far from the stay's town (tool design 2.5)." That is stated as settled, but tool design 2.5 doesn't say it. Issue #64 lists it as an open question, because many park attractions have no town in their short line. One example is Delicate Arch Trail, where `Place.town` is null for "Delicate Arch Trail, Utah, USA". The town can be missing for exactly the activities most likely to be far away. Saying the comment's claim is only a clue, and pointing to #64, would make it true.

**Why N5:** The comment overstates what the code gives, and the code right next to it is correct, so N5 fits. No agent reads this text, so F3 and N3 don't apply, and no design doc is wrong, so F6 doesn't apply.

Codify in DEVELOPMENT.md how issues are worked on autonomously, so Joe can say "work autonomously on #N" or "use subagents to work autonomously on #A and #B" without explaining it each time. When an issue has open questions, raise them and ask Joe whether to go through them first. Also clarify the comment in `src/tools/activity-lines.ts` that PR #202's review flagged.

## Results

- **DEVELOPMENT.md section 10** is new. It covers open questions, asking other questions up front, branches and worktrees, the order of PRs that depend on each other, decisions, when a PR is merged or held, and the report on all PRs at once.
- **DEVELOPMENT.md section 7** says asking for autonomous work counts as asking to merge the PRs section 10 allows.
- **CLAUDE.md** points to section 10.

## Decisions

- **"Check" findings hold a PR, the same as "fix" ones.** Joe asked for PRs to be held when a "fix" or "check" item is left. Written into DEVELOPMENT.md section 10.
- **Open questions left in an issue are raised before any other question.** Joe tries to settle them all before work starts, so one that's left was usually missed. Written into DEVELOPMENT.md section 10.

## Set aside

- Nothing.

## Config changes

None needed.

<!-- fix-loop: summary -->

## Fix loop: deferred, and needs attention

Code updates this comment after each fix round. Resolve a finding's thread once it's handled. A finding in a review body has no thread, so tick its box instead.

**Deferred**

None.

**Needs attention**

None.

**Fix (F6 - A design doc is wrong, so an agent building from it would build the wrong thing)**

Section 10 merges a PR only when it has the "ready for Joe" label, and holds any PR that never gets it. The "Code review" workflow (`.github/workflows/code-review.yml`, lines 17-19) runs only when a PR changes `src/**` or `web/**`. So a PR that changes only docs never gets a review, a fix loop, or the label. For example, an issue that ends in a design doc change, worked autonomously, opens its PR, and the session that "watches the loop" (line 226) waits for a loop that never starts. Section 10 doesn't say when to give up and call the PR held, or whether a docs-only PR may be merged without the label. Say how a PR that the workflow skips is handled, such as merging it once `npm run check` passes, or always holding it for Joe.

**Why F6:** This is a gap in the doc that an agent following section 10 would have to guess at, and a wrong guess leaves it waiting forever or merging against the rule. It isn't a false claim (D1) or a settled design point (D2), and it's a doc problem, not app behavior (F2).

**Fixed** in 282c48e7c88e619f8764f2b46b1059ab9941c4ee.

The claim holds. `.github/workflows/code-review.yml` runs only on PRs that change `src/**` or `web/**`, so a docs-only PR never gets the label. Section 10 already held "a PR that never gets the label", but it didn't say which PRs those are, or when to stop waiting. It now names two cases. A PR that changes nothing in `src/` or `web/` is held as soon as it's opened, with no loop to wait for. A PR whose "Code review" run fails is held too, since a failed review or fix job doesn't add the label. I chose holding over merging once `npm run check` passes, since holding is what the section already said, and merging unreviewed PRs would be a new policy for Joe to decide. No test, since this is a doc change.

**Note (N6 - A design doc is unclear, or doesn't match the code, in a way no builder would act on)**

Section 10 says decisions are made without Joe, even for "Settled in: chat", and its PRs merge without Joe's approval. But section 7 (line 119) still says a phase settled in the PR has Joe agree "by approving the PR", and section 9 (line 206) still says "chat" means proposing each answer to Joe first. Neither one mentions the exception in section 10. A reader of section 7 or 9 alone gets the old rule. A short "except as section 10 says" in each place would keep them from disagreeing.

**Why N6:** Section 10 states the override plainly, and CLAUDE.md sends autonomous work straight to section 10, so no one following the docs would act wrongly on it. That makes it a doc mismatch no builder would act on, rather than F6.

body:
Closes #198

## Do

- Add `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch` to the query's `tools`. Only worker definitions list the web tools, so the coordinator isn't sent them (tool design section 1).
- Add the two settings to the Claude Code process's environment: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` and `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` (technical spec 6.5).
- Add the `worker` server with `report_result` (tool design 2.6), built for each turn like the other servers, and add it to the query's `mcpServers`.
- Put `search_near` and `search_along_leg` on the `places` server. The coordinator's definition doesn't list them, so it isn't sent them.
- Set the query's `allowedTools` to each of our servers, plus `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch`, and write the reason into technical spec 6.5 (see the settled question above).
- Add the three hooks from technical spec 6.5: the `PostToolUse` hook that records each worker's calls by `agent_id`, the `SubagentStop` hook that sends a worker back at most twice when it hasn't called `report_result`, and the `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent` that replaces the worker's last message with the result code builds. Each acts only for our worker types (technical spec section 1).
- Draft the result's wording (technical spec 6.5), for Joe to review in the PR.

## Done when

- Tests with fake SDK messages show the `Agent` hook builds each kind of result: candidate replies in call order, a "No candidates added for:" line, a "No weather saved for:" line, problems and questions or "none", the last `report_result` call counting when there are two, and the line for a worker that stopped without reporting.
- Tests show the `SubagentStop` hook sends a worker back at most twice, and ignores agent types that aren't our workers.
- The coordinator's view file still shows no worker tool, such as `search_near` or `report_result`.

## Results

- **The `Agent` hook builds each kind of result.** Done. `src/agent/worker-hooks.test.ts` feeds the hooks the SDK's hook inputs over the Moab example, and checks: two candidate replies in call order, "No candidates added for:" with a stop and a stay's lodging, "No weather saved for:" for the weather worker, problems and questions, "none" for each when empty, the last of two `report_result` calls, and the line for a worker that stopped without reporting. It also checks that each of two workers gets only its own calls, that a call by the coordinator or another agent type isn't recorded, and that the output is left alone for another agent type or a worker that isn't done.
- **The `SubagentStop` hook sends a worker back at most twice, and ignores other agent types.** Done, in the same test file. A third stop is let through, each worker has its own count, a worker that reported is let stop, and `general-purpose` and `coordinator` are ignored.
- **The coordinator's view file still shows no worker tool.** Done. `npm run agent-views` left `src/agent/coordinator.view.md` unchanged.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Checked by hand

- **The hooks against the real SDK (0.3.301),** with a throwaway script, not committed: the coordinator as a named agent with `Agent(stay-researcher)`, a test worker on `claude-haiku-5-5` with `read_worker_brief_facts`, `add_stop_candidates`, and `report_result`, the real `trip` and `worker` servers over the Moab example in the fake store, and `workerHooks()`.
  - The `|` matcher reached the recording hook for each worker tool.
  - An MCP tool's reply reached `PostToolUse` as its list of content blocks, as the schema reads it.
  - A refused `add_stop_candidates` call (a made-up place ID) fired `PostToolUseFailure`, not `PostToolUse`, so it wasn't recorded.
  - The coordinator got the built result in place of the worker's message, with the reply, "No candidates added for:" naming the unfilled stop, and the problems and questions.
  - With the worker told never to call `report_result`, `SubagentStop` fired three times: sent back twice, then let through. The result ended with "The worker stopped without reporting its problems and questions."
- **One `npm run chat` turn against the local Postgres.** The turn ran with the new options. The tools the coordinator was sent were its 24 own tools, with no `Agent`, web tool, search, or `report_result`.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Each was made without Joe, as DEVELOPMENT.md section 10 says. Each is up for review here.

1. **The settled `allowedTools` answer is written into technical spec 6.5,** as a bullet beside the definitions, word for word from the issue's settled question, lightly trimmed.
2. **The result's wording is drafted in technical spec 6.5,** with a full example. Its old line, "The exact wording is drafted with the stay researcher (#60)", now says #198 drafted it. The wording is below.
3. **What got nothing is a list, one line each, after "No candidates added for:" or "No weather saved for:".** A stop's name has commas in it, such as `Day 2, Stop 1 (stop_…), attraction: "a sunrise hike"`, so several on one line would be hard to read. The list matches how "Problems:" lists its items. Written into technical spec 6.5.
4. **A stay with no lodging candidates is named "Lodging for Stay 1, Moab (stay_…)".** For the stay researcher, a missing stay means its lodging. For the weather worker, the stay is named alone, "Stay 2, Torrey (stay_…)". Each name is the one the tools already use (`stayName()` and `stopName()` in `src/tools/spot-names.ts`). Technical spec 6.5's old example, "Moab stay (stay_…)", changes to match. Written into technical spec 6.5.
5. **The parts of the result are separated by blank lines,** and the "No candidates added for:" part is left out when nothing is missing. A candidate reply is several lines, so a blank line shows where one ends. Written into technical spec 6.5.
6. **`report_result`'s questions input is `questionsForUser`, not `questions`.** The name says whose decision a question needs, so the model doesn't have to get that from its instructions alone. Written into tool design 2.6.
7. **`report_result`'s description says what the tool does and not to repeat what was added or saved.** It doesn't say what a problem and a question are. Tool design section 4 puts what an item means in the agent's instructions, and all three workers share it. Written into tool design 2.6. Moved to #60 as an open question (below).
8. **A hook that fails logs the error and changes nothing.** If the result can't be built, such as when the trip can't be read, the coordinator gets the worker's own last message, and the log says why. The other choice, throwing from the hook, has behavior the SDK doesn't document. Written into technical spec 6.5.
9. **A refused tool call isn't recorded.** A hand check showed it fires `PostToolUseFailure`, not `PostToolUse`. So the hook needs no check of its own. Written into technical spec 6.5.
10. **The worker types are in one place, `WORKER_TYPE` in `src/agent/worker-types.ts`,** with `isWorkerType()`, which the hooks use. #60 can use `WORKER_TYPE.stayResearcher` for its definition's key and its `Agent(...)` entry.
11. **The hooks name a stop or stay by reading the trip when the result is built.** It's read only when something got nothing. A stop or stay that's gone by then is named by its ID alone.
12. **DEVELOPMENT.md section 4 now lists the SDK's hook inputs** among the places outside data enters, checked with Zod. Its old line, "A worker returns text that the coordinator reads, not data our code parses", no longer held, since the hooks parse the worker's tool inputs and replies.

## The drafted result wording

**A stay researcher that filled the Moab stay's lodging and one stop, and found nothing for another:**

```
Lodging set 1 for Stay 1, Moab (stay_…): 3 candidates.
- Red Cliffs Lodge (place_…), Lodge, 4.5 stars, $$$, Moab. Why: "On the river, away from the busy main street." Tier: posh.
- Hoodoo Moab (place_…), Hotel, 4.4 stars, $$$, Moab. Why: "A short walk to the restaurants on Main Street." Tier: mid-range.
- Moab Springs Ranch (place_…), Lodge, 4.6 stars, $$, Moab. Why: "Quiet cottages at the edge of town." Tier: mid-range.

Set 1 for Day 2, Stop 4 (stop_…), meal: "burgers": 2 candidates.
- Milt's Stop & Eat (place_…), Hamburger restaurant, 4.6 stars, $, Moab. Why: "A classic burger stand since 1954." Tier: value.
- Moab Grill (place_…), American restaurant, 4.3 stars, $$, Moab. Why: "Big burgers, and seats for a sit-down lunch." Tier: value.

No candidates added for:
- Day 2, Stop 1 (stop_…), attraction: "a sunrise hike"

Problems:
- Only two burger places in Moab fit, so the Day 2 lunch has two candidates.
- The only sunrise hikes near Moab are already in the trip.
Questions for the user: none
```

**A worker that filled everything and has nothing to report:**

```
Set 1 for Day 2, Stop 4 (stop_…), meal: "burgers": 3 candidates.
- …

Problems: none
Questions for the user: none
```

**A worker with a question for the user:**

```
…

Problems: none
Questions for the user:
- Should the Day 2 lunch be a picnic, since the day is all hiking?
```

**The weather worker, with one stay saved and one missing.** `set_stay_weather` comes with #64, so its reply here is a placeholder:

```
<set_stay_weather's reply for Stay 1, Moab>

No weather saved for:
- Stay 2, Torrey (stay_…)

Problems:
- The forecast leaves out Torrey's last date, so I saved nothing for it.
Questions for the user: none
```

**A worker that never called `report_result`, even after being sent back twice:**

```
Set 1 for Day 2, Stop 4 (stop_…), meal: "burgers": 1 candidate.
- …

No candidates added for:
- Day 2, Stop 1 (stop_…), attraction: "a sunrise hike"

The worker stopped without reporting its problems and questions.
```

**What a worker is told when it tries to stop without reporting** (unchanged from technical spec 6.5): "You haven't called report_result. Call it now, with any problems and questions, to end your work."

**`report_result`'s description:** "Ends your work. Call it last, once your other calls are done, with your problems and your questions for the user. The coordinator gets what you added or saved from those calls, so don't repeat it here. A second call replaces the first." Its inputs: `problems` and `questionsForUser`, each "Short sentences, such as … [] when there are none." It replies "Result recorded. You're done."

## Set aside

- **What a problem and a question are, in the workers' instructions:** added to #60's open questions.
- **What `set_stay_weather` calls its stay ID input:** added to #64's open questions. The hooks read it as `stayId`, as `add_lodging_candidates` names it. A different name would list every stay as missing weather.
- **The `weather` server isn't in the session yet:** added to #64's open questions. `createWeatherServer()` exists, but no agent used it, so the query doesn't hold it.

## Config changes

None needed.

**Note (N3 - Text a road trip agent reads is unclear, or says something twice, or is an error message with the wrong reason for a failure)**

`WorkerCalls.record()` drops a repeated ID only when an earlier call already read it. It doesn't drop one that appears twice in the same `read_worker_brief_facts` call. The filter checks `record.readIds` before anything is pushed, so both copies get in. Example: a worker calls `read_worker_brief_facts` with `stopOrStayIds: ["stop_x", "stop_x"]` and adds nothing to `stop_x`. The coordinator then sees `stop_x` listed twice under "No candidates added for:". Running `record('a1', 'mcp__trip__read_worker_brief_facts', {stopOrStayIds: ['stop_x','stop_x']}, [])` leaves `readIds` as `['stop_x', 'stop_x']`. The tool itself counts a repeated ID once (`factsLines` in `worker-brief-facts-tool.ts` uses `new Set`), and the `WorkerRecord` comment says "each once". Removing duplicates within the call too, such as with `new Set([...record.readIds, ...ids])`, would fix it.

**Why N3:** The result the coordinator reads names the same stop twice, so it says something twice. That is N3. Nothing in it is false, so it isn't F3, and the worker's work is still reported correctly, so the coordinator wouldn't act wrongly on it, which rules out F2.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

These were made without Joe, as DEVELOPMENT.md section 10 says, though the issue says "Settled in: chat".

- **What a problem and a question are, for `report_result`.** The last open question, settled with its proposal. One block of text, `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts`, that every worker includes word for word. A problem is something the coordinator should know that it can't tell from what the worker saved. A question needs the user's decision, and is asked only when the worker can't do an item well without the answer. Each is a short sentence that names stops and stays as the tools do. The worker doesn't list what it saved, or say all went well. The examples are tool design 2.6's, plus one for "nothing at the tier asked for". **Why:** all three workers share the meaning, and tool design section 4 puts shared rules in one block of code that each prompt includes. Written into technical spec 6.4, with a pointer from tool design 2.6, and struck out in the issue body.
- **The candidate-field block also gives each tier's meaning.** `CANDIDATE_FIELDS` covers `howFound` with `sourceLink`, `rationale`, `notes`, and `visitTimeInMinutes`, as settled, and also `tier`: functional spec 7.1's meanings, by the names the tool takes (`value`, `midRange`, `upscale`), and the price level as a guide. **Why:** `tier` is a candidate field too, and the leg scout labels meals with the same meanings, so it belongs in the block the leg scout reuses. Written into technical spec 6.1.
- **A worker model setting, `workerModel`, set to `claude-sonnet-5-5`.** One setting for every worker. **Why:** a definition with no model can get a default subagent model, so it needs an exact ID, like the coordinator's. Workers judge tiers and fit places to the user's words, which needs more than the smallest model. Several run at once in the fill, so Opus would use up the plan quickly. One setting until an evaluation shows a worker needs its own. Written into technical spec section 10, and the 6.5 bullet on each worker's definition.
- **The coordinator lays out the stops, tells the user, and sends the workers once the user is happy with the stops.** Technical spec 4.2 says the coordinator lays out the stops and then briefs the workers, without saying whether the user sees the stops first. **Why:** a worker run costs searches and model calls, and the functional spec's conduct rule is "don't make choices silently." In the chat check, the user had already said "go ahead", so the coordinator sent them in the same turn. Written into technical spec 5.2, "When to send work to a worker".
- **When to send a worker again:** when the user asks for more options, or for something nicer or simpler, or has turned down every candidate. **Why:** technical spec 5.2's rejection bullet already says a worker is needed only when none are left or the user asks for more. It needed to be in the prompt now that there are workers. Written into technical spec 5.2.
- **What the coordinator does with a worker's result.** It tells the user briefly what was found, recommends where it helps, doesn't list every candidate (the option card shows them), raises the problems, asks the questions, and offers choices when a stop got nothing. The instructions also say what each part of the result means. **Why:** tool design section 4 says the instructions explain a reply's lines, and the meal coverage answer says the coordinator tells the user when a worker found nothing. Written into technical spec 5.2.
- **Until the leg scout, stops along a leg or near the start or end place get no worker.** The coordinator leaves them empty, and tells the user they can name a place. **Why:** the meal default puts lunch along the leg on driving days, and the coordinator has no worker for it yet. Without the line, it might send the stay researcher for them, and `search_near` refuses a stop along the leg. #61 replaces the line (added to its Do). Written into technical spec 5.2.
- **The meal coverage answer is now in the design and the prompt.** The settled question said to write it into technical spec 5.2, under laying out a day, and functional spec 7.3. Neither had it, so this PR adds both, and the "Laying out days" section of the prompt.
- **Hours for a place found on the web come from `search_near`, searched by name.** `find_place` gives no hours or rating, and the stay researcher has no `read_place`. **Why:** this uses the tools as they are, and `search_near` gives hours on the stop's own date. Written into technical spec 6.1.
- **The stay researcher is told nobody reads its own messages,** so it keeps them short. **Why:** code builds the result from its calls (technical spec 6.5), so its text costs tokens and does nothing. Written into technical spec 6.1.
- **Two lines added after the chat check.** The Moab researcher offered the same Mexican places for two dinners, and reported it as a problem for the user to sort out. So the instructions now say to give each meal its own places, and to offer one place for two meals only when too few fit, and report it. It also put "Hours not confirmed" in a motel's notes, so the instructions now say hours are for stops only. **Why:** both came straight from the instructions as written. Written into technical spec 6.1.
- **The coordinator's view lists the worker types** under "Worker types", in the same line format Claude Code uses: "- stay-researcher: description (Tools: …)". The test builds it from the coordinator's `Agent(...)` entry and each named definition. `toolsOn()` moved to `src/agent/tool-names.ts`, since both definitions use it.
- **The rationale example drops "fits mid-range"** in domain model 3.9 and technical spec 7.2, as the settled question said. Technical spec 7.2 now says why: the card shows the tier.

## The worker brief outline (technical spec 5.3), for Joe to review

The coordinator writes each worker brief under these headings, in this order. Every heading is always there, with "none" under one that has nothing for the worker. The headings are `WORKER_BRIEF_HEADING` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts`, and both prompts use them.

```
Fill:
- each stop ID, and the stay's ID when its lodging needs candidates, one per line
When:
- each stop, with roughly when the coordinator expects it, in plain words
Lodging preferences:
the user's words on places to stay that apply to this stay, from the trip brief and memory, quoted, and the coordinator's reading where it's clear
Meal preferences:
the same for food, for the meal stops in this worker brief
Interests and must-sees:
the ones that apply to these stops, in the user's words
Avoid:
what memory says to avoid, such as "no chain restaurants"
Request:
what the user asked for when a worker is sent for one stop or stay again, such as "something nicer than these"
```

- **A stay's ID under "Fill:" means its lodging.** The `Agent` hook lists a stay with no lodging candidates as missing, so a stay whose lodging is already selected gets only its stops' IDs.
- **The coordinator's example is a Camden stay on the Natick to Bar Harbor trip.** It shows the B&B wish going to Camden, since no town has a B&B yet. It isn't Moab, so the chat check and any later evaluation don't reward a copied answer.
- **The coordinator's instructions also say:** pass the user's own words, not only a tier. Ask the user first when it's unclear what their words cover. Send a wish that covers more than one stay to each of those stays' workers until one of them has it, so check the selected lodging first. Never copy all of memory into a worker brief.
- **In the chat check, the coordinator followed it well.** Example, the Torrey brief:

  ```
  Fill:
  - stay_akq7cr5p
  - stop_n6k5svzk
  - stop_wkh3sxaa
  When:
  - stop_n6k5svzk: after Goblin Valley and a hike in Capitol Reef, they reach Torrey in the late afternoon, so this is dinner, around 6:00 p.m.
  - stop_wkh3sxaa: stargazing after dinner, set for 8:30 p.m., in October, about 1–2 hours.
  Lodging preferences:
  "in Torrey, anything clean and simple is fine since it's one night." Hotel breakfast is welcome if offered.
  Meal preferences:
  "Hotel breakfast is fine, for lunch and dinner we like casual local places, burgers and Mexican, nothing fancy."
  Interests and must-sees:
  "We love hiking and stargazing." Capitol Reef is an International Dark Sky Park; a dark, easy-to-reach spot near Torrey or in Capitol Reef suits the stargazing, with easy footing (partner recovering from a knee injury), and an easy drive after dark.
  Avoid:
  none
  Request:
  none
  ```

## Set aside, and where

- **#61, the leg scout:** its Do now says to include `CANDIDATE_FIELDS` and `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` word for word, and to replace the coordinator's line that says stops along a leg have no worker yet, in the prompt and in technical spec 5.2.
- **#64, the weather worker:** its Do now says to include `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` word for word.
- **The repeat-places fix wasn't rerun** on a fresh fill. The Torrey rerun after the fix checked only the lodging-hours fix. Nothing to track: the next fill in a chat or an evaluation shows it.

## Config changes

None needed. `settings.json` is the app's settings file, not one of the config files in DEVELOPMENT.md section 6.

**Note (N3 - Text a road trip agent reads is unclear, or says something twice, or is an error message with the wrong reason for a failure)**

PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS tells each worker to "Name stops and stays as the tools do, such as \"Day 2, Stop 4\" or \"the Moab stay\"." The tools don't name a stay "the Moab stay". stayName() in src/tools/spot-names.ts names it "Stay 1, Moab (stay_…)", and the candidate tools' replies use that form, such as "Lodging set 1 for Stay 1, Moab". So the example contradicts the rule it illustrates. A worker that follows the example writes problems such as "the Moab stay has only two lodging candidates", while the rest of the result says "Stay 1, Moab". This text is shared word for word with the leg scout and the weather worker.

**Why N3:** The text is unclear, since its example contradicts its own rule. It isn't a false claim an agent would act on wrongly, because the coordinator can still tell which stay is meant, so it falls below F3. It isn't D1, D2 or D3: the claim is true, the design (technical spec 6.4) gives only "Day 2, Stop 4" as the example, and no issue takes this on.

title: The stay researcher

body:
## Task

Follow-up changes Joe asked for after PRs #205 (issue #198, the worker setup and hooks) and #207 (issue #60, the stay researcher) merged.

1. **A failed result build is reported, not hidden.** Today `logged()` in `src/agent/worker-hooks.ts` catches an error from a hook, logs it, and returns `{}`. For the `Agent` hook that replaces a worker's last message, that lets the worker's own free text reach the coordinator, with no sign anything failed. Change it so that when building the result throws, the hook still replaces the worker's message, with one line that includes the error's message, such as: "Code failed to build this worker's result, so the result isn't available. The error: <the error's message>." It can't list the stops and stays, since that's the code that failed. Keep logging the error. If the SDK's `Agent` output itself isn't the shape needed to build a replacement, log and return `{}` as today. The other hooks (recording calls, sending back) keep today's behavior. Add a line to the coordinator's instructions, where they say what a worker's result holds (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`): when a result says code failed to build it, tell the user the error as written. This is for Joe's testing and learning, so the user seeing the raw error is wanted. Update technical spec 6.5, which says today that a failed hook changes nothing.
2. **A model and effort setting for each agent.** Replace the one `workerModel` setting with a model setting and an effort setting for each agent that exists: the coordinator and the stay researcher. The stay researcher keeps `claude-sonnet-5-5`. The coordinator keeps its model. Each agent's definition gets its model and its effort (the SDK's `AgentDefinition` has `effort?: 'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'|'max'|number`; see `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts`). For the coordinator, which is the session's main agent, set the effort the same way its model is set today (technical spec 6.5 sets the model both in the query options and the definition, so nothing depends on which the SDK reads); check whether the query `Options` has an `effort` too. Start each effort at the level the agent runs at today, written out, so this change doesn't change what any agent does; find that default in the SDK's types/docs, and say in the decisions comment how you found it. Show each agent's model and effort at the top of its view file (`src/agent/agent-views.test.ts`, then `npm run agent-views`), so a PR's diff shows a change. Write the settings into technical spec section 10 and the reason into 6.5: each agent has its own, so one agent's model or effort can change and be evaluated alone. The leg scout (#61) and weather worker (#64) add their own settings in their issues; don't add them here.
3. **"posh" is now "upscale".** Technical spec 6.5's example result says "Tier: posh." Change it to "Tier: upscale." Also check `design/`, `src/`, `web/`, and the root docs for any other "posh"; leave `research/`, `reviews/`, and `plan/` alone, since those are records of the past.
4. **A repeated ID in one `read_worker_brief_facts` call is recorded once.** `WorkerCalls.record()` in `src/agent/worker-calls.ts` skips an ID that an earlier call already read, but not one repeated in the same call. So `["stay_a", "stop_x", "stop_x"]`, with nothing added to `stop_x`, lists that stop twice under "No candidates added for:". Record each ID once.
5. **The shared problems-and-questions text names stays the way the tools do.** `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts` says: Name stops and stays as the tools do, such as "Day 2, Stop 4" or "the Moab stay". The tools name a stay "Stay 1, Moab". Change the example to "Stay 1, Moab", and fix the same example anywhere in `design/`.

Items 1 and 4 are bug fixes, so each comes with a test that fails without the fix and passes with it, through the path where the bug was (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5). Check each test against the code without the fix. Every agent's view file is rewritten in the same commit as the change to what it sees.

## Results

1. **Done.** When building the result throws, the `Agent` hook now replaces the worker's message with "Code failed to build this worker's result, so the result isn't available. The error: <message>", and still logs the error. An `Agent` output that isn't the right shape still logs and changes nothing. The coordinator's instructions now say to tell the user the error as written, and technical spec 6.5 says what each failure does. Test: `worker-hooks.test.ts`, "says code failed to build the result…", which makes the trip read fail while the stop that got nothing is named. It failed on the code without the fix (the hook left the worker's own message) and passes with it. A second test covers an `Agent` output with no `agentId`.
2. **Done.** `workerModel` is replaced by `coordinatorModel`, `coordinatorEffort`, `stayResearcherModel`, and `stayResearcherEffort`. Both efforts start at `medium`, the level each agent runs at today. The coordinator's effort is set in the query's `Options.effort` and in its definition. Each view file now starts with its model and effort. Technical spec section 10 has the settings, and 6.5 has the reason. A test gives each agent a different model and effort, and checks that each reaches only that agent.
3. **Done.** Technical spec 6.5's example now says "Tier: upscale." No other "posh" in `design/`, `src/`, `web/`, or the root docs.
4. **Done.** Each ID is recorded once, even when one call repeats it. Test: `worker-hooks.test.ts`, "lists a stop once when one read_worker_brief_facts call names it twice". It failed on the code without the fix (the stop was listed twice) and passes with it.
5. **Done.** The example is now "Stay 1, Moab", and the stay researcher's view file is rewritten. No design doc had the same example.

`npm run check` passes.

## Checked by hand

- **The effort each agent runs at today.** A small query against the plan, set up like the app's (a named main agent on `claude-opus-5-5`, a worker on `claude-sonnet-5-5`, adaptive thinking, no settings files), logged the `effort` field of the `PostToolUse` hook inputs. With no effort set, both the main agent and the worker said `medium`. With effort set in the options and definitions (`low` for the main agent, `high` for the worker), each said the level set for it. Agent SDK 0.3.301.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

**Failed result build (item 1)**

- **The exact line is "Code failed to build this worker's result, so the result isn't available. The error: " plus the error's message.** Line breaks and runs of spaces in the message become one space, so it stays one line. A Zod error's message is pretty-printed JSON over many lines. Written into technical spec 6.5.
- **The first sentence is one constant, `BUILD_FAILED_LINE` in `worker-result.ts`, and the coordinator's instructions import it.** So the text the coordinator is told to look for can't drift from the text the hook writes. `RESUMED_LINE` works the same way.
- **The coordinator's new line:** "Code failed to build this worker's result, so the result isn't available." means the app hit an error, so you can't tell what the worker saved. Tell the user the error as written, after "The error:". It says what the coordinator doesn't know, so it doesn't guess at what was saved.
- **The catch sits around the build only, in `resultOrFailure()`.** Parsing the `Agent` input and output stays outside it, so a bad output still falls through to `logged()`, which logs and returns `{}`. A test covers that case too (an output with no `agentId`), since the task names it.
- **The test makes the trip read fail.** That's the one outside call the build makes, when it names a stop that got nothing. It goes through the hook `workerHooks()` returns, with `logged()` around it.

**Model and effort settings (item 2)**

- **The settings are `coordinatorModel`, `coordinatorEffort`, `stayResearcherModel`, and `stayResearcherEffort`.** Same pattern as the existing `coordinatorModel`, one pair per agent. Written into technical spec section 10.
- **Both efforts start at `medium`.** The SDK's types and the docs they link don't give a default level. So I checked by hand. The hook inputs carry an `effort.level` field ("the active effort level for the current turn, after any silent downgrade"). I ran a small query set up like the app's: a named main agent on `claude-opus-5-5`, a worker on `claude-sonnet-5-5`, adaptive thinking, no settings files. With no effort set, both said `medium`. With `low` set for the main agent and `high` for the worker, each said what was set. So setting `medium` changes nothing, and an explicit setting does take effect. Written into technical spec 6.5.
- **The coordinator's effort goes in both the query's `Options.effort` and its definition.** `Options` has `effort?: EffortLevel`. Setting both matches how its model is set, so nothing depends on which the SDK reads. Written into technical spec 6.5.
- **The setting takes named levels only, not a number.** `AgentDefinition.effort` takes a number too, but `Options.effort` doesn't, and the coordinator's has to go in both. One schema for all agents keeps it simple.
- **The view file shows the model and effort from the agent's definition.** For the coordinator, the query's options have the same values, and `coordinator.test.ts` checks that.
- **Technical spec 5.4 gets one sentence:** the coordinator's effort setting guides how much it thinks. DEVELOPMENT.md section 5 now says a view file starts with the agent's model and effort.

**Other items**

- **Technical spec 6.5's example also says "Tier: midRange." in place of "Tier: mid-range."** The tool writes the tier's stored name (`Tier: ${candidate.tier}` in `stop-lines.ts`), so "mid-range" was wrong in the same way "posh" was.
- **Item 5: no design doc had the "the Moab stay" example.** Technical spec 6.4 gives only "Day 2, Stop 4", which is right, so I left it.
- **The worker hooks test's helpers moved to `worker-hooks.fake.ts`.** The new tests took the test file over the 300-line limit. The Zod schema that checks the replaced output stays in the test file, since lint allows Zod only in schema and test files.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes needed

None.

title: Worker follow-ups from #198 and #60

body:
## Task

Closes #194.

### Do

- Settle each open question.
- Make each change: the app's date line and the coordinator's instructions, technical spec 5.2, the view files and DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, the Claude Code process's environment, and the traces and systems design section 10.
- Rewrite each changed view file with `npm run agent-views`.

### Done when

- Each open question is answered, and its answer is written into the doc it belongs to.
- The coordinator never reads two different dates for today.
- Each turn's span holds the commit SHA of the code that ran, with `-dirty` on a local run with uncommitted changes.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Results

- **Each open question is answered and written in.** All were settled in the issue before the work started. The date answer is in technical spec 5.2. The git status setting is in technical spec 6.5. The view file note is in DEVELOPMENT.md section 5. The trace answers (the commit, no system prompt or added text in the trace, no worker tool list) are in systems design section 10, with the image's commit in section 7. Phoenix's prompt registry was already an open question in #53.
- **The coordinator never reads two different dates.** Each turn's Claude Code process now runs with `TZ` set to the app's date line's time zone: the start place's, or UTC until there is one. Both come from one function, `tripTimeZone()`. Tests in `chat-turns.test.ts`: a new trip runs in UTC, and the Moab trip at 7 p.m. in Grand Junction gets "Today is Thursday, October 15, 2026." with `TZ=America/Denver`, while UTC is already October 16. Both tests failed with the old code, where `TZ` wasn't set.
- **Each turn's span holds the commit.** It's `commit` in the `coordinator.turn` span's `metadata`. On the server, the deploy passes `APP_COMMIT` into the app image. Locally, the app asks git when it starts, and adds `-dirty` when `git status` shows any change, new files included.
- **`npm run check` passes.**

Also: `claudeProcessEnv()` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1`, and both view files start with the note about Claude Code's added text.

## Checked by hand

- **The app image carries the commit.** Built `docker/app.Dockerfile` with `--build-arg APP_COMMIT=abc123`: `printenv APP_COMMIT` in the container gave `abc123`. Built without the argument, it gave `unknown`.
- **A local turn's trace has the commit.** Ran one turn with `npm run chat` on this branch, with uncommitted changes. Phoenix's `road-trip-agent-local` project showed `metadata.commit` = `6b0dbee8c8dc00b155689017850c82fffcefb23c-dirty` on the turn's span.
- **Not checked live:** that Claude Code's date line follows `TZ`. #188 already showed that (research section 2.9), and this change only sets the variable.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **The app's date line and the coordinator's instructions stay as they are.** The issue's "Do" names them, but the settled date answer keeps the app's line, since Claude Code's has no weekday. With `TZ` set, Claude Code's date always matches the app's, so the instructions have nothing to explain. Written into technical spec 5.2.
- **The commit goes in the turn span's `metadata`, as `commit`, not as a plain attribute.** Phoenix shows `metadata` on its own tab and can filter on it. Phoenix stores it as `metadata.commit`, which the hand check confirmed. Written into systems design section 10.
- **The commit is built into the app image, as `APP_COMMIT`, not set by `ops/deploy.sh`.** Then the image itself says which commit it is. That stays true when someone rolls back by hand, by tagging an earlier image as `:latest` (systems design section 7). The `ARG` is the last step of the image, so a new commit rebuilds only that layer. Written into systems design sections 7 and 10.
- **A local build of the whole Compose stack says `unknown`.** The image has no git and no `.git` folder, so it can't ask. The Dockerfile's default is `unknown`, so a local stack still starts. Written into systems design section 10.
- **New files count as uncommitted changes.** The app checks `git status --porcelain`, not `git describe --dirty`, which skips untracked files. A new `.ts` file changes what runs, so the view files at the commit may not match. Written into systems design section 10.
- **Locally, if git can't give the commit, the app stops at start,** with a `ConfigError`, as with a missing environment value. `npm run dev` and `npm run chat` always run from the repo, so this shouldn't happen.
- **`APP_COMMIT` is in the environment schema, as the one optional value,** since only the image sets it.

## Set aside

- Nothing. I also dropped a stale line in systems design section 10 that said no worker exists yet.

## Config changes

- None. `docker/app.Dockerfile` and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` changed, but neither is in the DEVELOPMENT.md section 6 list.

All three were checked in one `npm run chat` session against the local Postgres, with real Claude and Google: session `session_ahh7vvfr` on trip `trip_wuptjt75`, for a new user (`6b1d2c3e-6161-4a61-8b61-000000000061`). The trip was built from domain model 5.1: San Francisco to Mike's house in Silver Lake from May 13, 2027, a night in Monterey and one in San Luis Obispo, scenic on Highway 1, and fastest on Day 3.

- **The leg scout for San Francisco Day 2 fills Point Lobos, Bixby Creek, and lunch with candidates that have detour times.** Done. The coordinator first selected Point Lobos and Bixby Creek Bridge itself, since they were must-sees. So I asked it to leave those two stops without a place, and let the scout find options.
