body:
## Do

- Change functional spec 5.2, technical spec 5.2 and 10, and the domain model to match the answers. Remove `restDaysText` from the trip brief's code, its tool input, and its saved form.
- Add a migration that removes `restDaysText` from the trip brief in every saved trip's plan, as `migrations/0008_drop_stay_tier_nights.sql` does for its keys.
- Add the default comfortable driving hours setting, 4 hours, to the settings and technical spec section 10. A new trip's trip brief starts with it, as it starts with the usual start time.
- **Ask first the questions the trip sketches need.** In turn 1, the coordinator's reply asked 7 numbered questions, though the instructions say "Ask a few questions at a time." Joe answered the ones the sketches needed, and the sketches in turn 2 came out well. Have the coordinator ask first the few questions it needs to offer the trip sketches, and the rest later. Raised by Joe. Moved here from #231 on 2026-10-30, since it also decides which questions discovery asks, and when. Write it together with dropping driving hours and rest days from discovery, so the two read as one rule.
- Change the coordinator's instructions in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`, and the `update_trip_brief` description if the default changes what it says. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Asked by Joe after #238 merged: fix #238's review note on the coordinator's read line for "Named by the user". Stops selected before #238 don't say when the place was the coordinator's suggestion, so the coordinator mustn't take that as proof the user named it.

## Done when

- The coordinator's instructions say when to raise driving hours and rest days, and to ask first the questions the trip sketches need. The design docs match.
- A trip saved before the change loads after `npm run migrate`, run locally.
- `npm run check` passes.


Closes #230

## Results

- **The coordinator's instructions say when to raise driving hours and rest days, and to ask first the questions the trip sketches need. The design docs match.** Done. "The trip brief" section now says to ask first only what the sketches need, and not to ask about driving hours or rest days during discovery, in one list. "Comfortable driving hours" says the item starts at the default and that the daily driving check's warning is the cue to ask. "Days and approvals" says when to offer a rest day. Functional spec 5.2, 5.3, and S1 and S9, technical spec 4.2, 5.2, 8, and 10, and domain model 3.1, 3.2, and the stay day table match. `src/agent/coordinator.view.md` is rewritten. The `update_trip_brief` description didn't need a change.
  - Checked by hand: one `npm run chat` turn against a migrated copy of the local database, with the opening message of the Bar Harbor session. The dev user's memory holds "Comfortable driving about 5 hours a day". The coordinator set the trip brief's hours to 5 and said so in one line, offered three sketches, and asked four questions, all for the sketches. It asked nothing about driving hours, route preference, meals, lodging, or a rest day.
- **A trip saved before the change loads after `npm run migrate`, run locally.** Done, against a copy of the local database (`pg_dump` into a separate database), so the other branches using the shared local Postgres still load their trips. All 15 saved trips held `restDaysText`, and 9 had no comfortable driving hours.
  - Before the migration, the new code's reader failed on all 15, with "Unrecognized key: restDaysText".
  - After `npm run migrate` ran `0010_trip_brief_driving_and_rest_days`, all 15 loaded through `TripReader`. The 9 empty ones now read 4, and the others kept theirs (4, 5, or 6).
  - Each plan, minus those two keys, hashes the same before and after, so nothing else changed.
  - A trip started with the new code through `TripWriter.startTrip` reads back with `comfortableDrivingInHours: 4`, and no `restDaysText` in its saved form.
- **`npm run check` passes.** Done.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **Comfortable driving hours is never empty now, like the usual start time.** It's a plain `number` in the trip brief, not `{keepsValue}`, the saved form requires it, and the daily driving check no longer skips a trip without it. Every new trip starts with the default, so an empty value could only come from an old trip. Keeping the empty case would leave a "not set" that the instructions say can't happen. Written in domain model 3.2 and technical spec 8.
- **The migration also sets an empty comfortable driving hours to 4.** The saved form now requires a value. And an old trip without one would never get the daily driving check, since the coordinator no longer asks for it. The 4 is written into the SQL as the setting's starting value, since a migration runs once. 9 of the 15 local trips had none. Written in the migration's comment and technical spec 10.
- **The new setting is `defaultComfortableDrivingHours`, and the app won't start when it's over the maximum daily driving.** A new trip's trip brief would otherwise break its own limit. `newTrip()` takes it from the settings, so tests pass `EXAMPLE_SETTINGS`. Written in technical spec 10.
- **When user memory holds the user's usual driving hours, the coordinator sets them and says so in one line, without a question.** The settled answer says no driving hours question in discovery, and functional spec 10.3 says to confirm rather than re-ask. S9 now says the agent plans with the usual hours and says so. Written in technical spec 5.2 and functional spec 5.2 and S9.
- **The instructions say not to raise comfortable driving hours to cover one long day.** In the Bar Harbor session, the coordinator set 6 hours itself to cover Day 1. That's why Saturday's 5½ hours raised no warning. The settled answer gives "that day is fine" an approval instead. Written in technical spec 5.2.
- **The order of questions.** First what the sketches need: the focus, trip length, interests and must-sees, start and end places, and start date. Then the route preference before the skeleton, and meal and lodging preferences before the fill. In turn 1 of the Bar Harbor session, those first items are the ones Joe answered before the sketches came out well. The route preference matters first for the skeleton's scenic waypoints, and the meal and lodging preferences first for the worker briefs. The usual start time isn't in the list, since it has a default. Written in technical spec 5.2 and functional spec 5.2.
- **"Never suggest more than the recommended daily driving on your own" names sketches and skeletons.** Those are where the coordinator proposes days. Written in technical spec 5.2.
- **When a night that was a rest day the user asked for is removed, the coordinator updates or forgets the memory item that asked for it.** That replaces updating `restDaysText`. Written in technical spec 5.2.
- **Functional spec 5.2 marks comfortable driving hours as not required.** It starts with a default, as the usual start time does, and the agent doesn't ask for it.
- **The trip brief, trip length, and comfortable driving hours sections moved to `src/agent/coordinator-trip-brief-prompt.ts`.** With the new text, `coordinator-prompt.ts` went over the 300-line lint limit. This follows `coordinator-choices-prompt.ts` and `coordinator-weather-prompt.ts`. The text the coordinator sees is the same as if it had stayed. #231 also edits `coordinator-prompt.ts`, so this will need a merge.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes

None needed.

**Fix (F6 - A design doc is wrong, so an agent building from it would build the wrong thing)**

Technical spec 5.2 tells the coordinator: "When user memory holds the user's usual driving hours, the coordinator sets the trip brief's comfortable driving hours to them." The prompt says the same at src/agent/coordinator-trip-brief-prompt.ts:69. The rule has no condition, such as "on a new trip" or "while the brief still holds the default". The coordinator reads the brief and memory at the start of every session, so the rule fires in every session, not only the first one. Now that comfortableDrivingInHours is never empty, the coordinator can't tell the 4-hour default from a 4 the user chose. Here is a concrete case, from acceptance scenario S10. User memory says 6 hours. On this trip the user says "only 4 hours a day this time", and says it's a one-off. The brief holds 4. User memory stays at 6. Trip memory doesn't record the override, since the memory rule says not to save to trip memory what the brief holds. In the next session on this trip, the coordinator reads a brief of 4 and a memory of 6, and follows the rule. It sets comfortableDrivingInHours to 6 and says "I've planned on your usual 6 hours". That undoes what the user asked for. The precedence rule (conversation, then trip memory, then user memory) doesn't stop it, since it doesn't mention the brief. Before this PR, the brief was empty until the user answered, so a set value always meant the user had chosen it.

**Why F6:** The prompt does what the design asks, but the design's rule overrides a choice the user made for this trip, in a later session, which is normal use. So it's F6 and not D2. It isn't F1, since the task's wording is followed.

**Fixed** in be1fbab.
The coordinator sets the hours from user memory only on a new trip, while its focus is empty. After that, the trip brief's value stands.

**Note (N2 - A missing test)**

The test checks that defaultComfortableDrivingHours is filled in only through "comfortableDrivingInHours starts at 3 hours", which is in the Comfortable driving hours section. The trip brief section's item line also uses the setting: "It's ${startingHours} hours until the user says otherwise". Nothing checks that line. If it were written as a hard-coded "It's 4 hours", the test would still pass. The comment says 4 can't be searched for because of text such as "Stop 4".

**Why N2:** The test checks the real thing but misses one of the two places the setting is used. That's a missing case, so it's N2, not F7.

**Fixed** in be1fbab.
The test now checks the trip brief's item line too.

**Note (N3 - Text a road trip agent reads is unclear, or says something twice, or is an error message with the wrong reason for a failure)**

The "Changes to stays" rule says that when the user agrees to lose a rest day, the coordinator should "update or forget the memory item that asked for it". It doesn't say which memory. Under this PR, a rest day can come from trip memory, such as "one day off in Moab". It can also come from a standing habit in user memory, such as "we always take a day off mid-trip". Here is a concrete case. The user's memory says they always take a day off mid-trip. On a 7-day trip, the coordinator marks Day 4 as a rest day. Later the user removes a night and agrees to lose that rest day for this trip. Read alone, the rule points the coordinator at the user memory item, so it could forget a standing habit because of a change on one trip. The memory precedence rule, which says to ask whether something applies to this trip only, probably stops this. But the rule here should say what to do when the item is in user memory, such as saving a trip-only note in trip memory instead.

**Why N3:** The memory precedence rule in the same instructions makes the coordinator ask before it changes user memory, so false text leading to a wrong action is unlikely. That makes this unclear text (N3), not F3 or F6. Technical spec 5.2 uses the same wording, but D2 doesn't fit, since the design doesn't speak to which memory is meant.

**Fixed** in be1fbab.
The rule now updates or forgets the trip memory item. A standing habit in user memory stays, with a note for this trip in trip memory.

**Note (N2 - A missing test)**

The startTrip test checks that a new trip's comfortableDrivingInHours is 4. The test settings' defaultComfortableDrivingHours is also 4 (example-trip-parts.fake.ts:38). So if newTrip() ignored the setting and hard-coded 4, the test would still pass. The same is true of the read_trip_brief test that expects "comfortableDrivingInHours: 4". If the test settings used a value other than the starting one, such as 3, the test would show that the brief takes its value from the setting.

**Why N2:** The test does check the default, but it misses the case that tells the setting apart from a hard-coded 4. That's a missing case, N2, not a wrong test (F7).

**Fixed** in be1fbab.
The startTrip test gives the setting 3, unlike settings.json's 4.

Line 1028.

**Note (N6 - A design doc is unclear, or doesn't match the code, in a way no builder would act on)**

TripBriefService.setComfortableDriving() still lists "or is empty" among the brief's own rules that refuse a value. This PR makes comfortableDrivingInHours a plain `decimal` that is never empty. The setter takes a `number`, and the tool input is optional, so an empty value never reaches it. The doc now describes a refusal that can't happen.

**Why N6:** The doc no longer matches the code. But section 3.2 of the same doc says the item is never empty, so no builder would add an empty check because of this. That makes it N6, not F6.

**Fixed** in be1fbab.
Removed "or is empty".

body:
## Do

- Add a table for trip versions, with a migration: one row per turn, keyed to its session and its turn.
- Save a version at the start of every coordinator turn, in `CoordinatorTurns` (`src/agent/coordinator-turns.ts`), which both the app's API and `npm run chat` use. Save it after the checks that can refuse the turn, such as a closed chat or a turn already running, so a refused message saves nothing.
- Remove a trip's versions in `TripWriter.deleteTrip()`.
- Write trip versions into the persistence design: what a version holds, when it's saved, and that a trip's delete removes them.
- Add tests with fake repositories (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).

## Done when

- A session with three turns on the local stack (systems design, section 6) has three versions. Each matches the trip as it stood when its turn started. Check it by hand by forgetting a memory item between turns 2 and 3: the item is in version 2 and not in version 3.
- Deleting the trip removes its versions.
- `npm run check` passes.

Closes #243

## Results

- **Three turns, three versions: done.** I ran three turns with `npm run chat` against the local Postgres, on a new trip for a new dev user. Turn 1 saved a user memory item ("Loves breweries."). Turn 2 set the start date and start place, and saved a trip memory item. Between turns 2 and 3, I removed the brewery item's row, as forgetting it does. Then turn 3 ran.
  - Version 1 has no memory and no places: the new trip, before the coordinator ran.
  - Version 2 has "Loves breweries." and not the trip item, which turn 2 added.
  - Version 3 has the trip item and not "Loves breweries.", and holds the start date and the Portland place.
  - Before turns 2 and 3, I copied the trip's plan (and before turn 3, its places) into a scratch table. Version 2's plan equals the copy taken before turn 2. Version 3's plan and places equal the copy taken before turn 3.
  - The forget was a SQL `DELETE` of the item's row, not the chat view's memory list. `MemoryWriter.forget()` removes the row the same way.
- **Deleting the trip removes its versions: done.** I ran `TripRepository.remove()` on that trip, in a transaction. Afterward the session had 0 versions, and the trip and session rows were gone.
- **`npm run check`: passes,** 923 tests.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

All of these are written into the persistence design, section 8.9, unless noted.

- **A version copies the stored rows, in one SQL statement.** It copies the trip's `plan` column, its place rows, and the memory item rows `MemoryReader.read()` would return, each row turned into JSON with its column names. Why: one statement reads everything at the same moment, with no lock. Restoring a version is then a copy back into the tables. And since the app never reads versions, there's no need to build domain objects or parse them with Zod here.
- **The turn number counts the user's messages in the coordinator's transcript, as the browser shows them, plus one.** It's `userMessageCount()`, next to `shownMessagesOf()` in `src/agent/shown-messages.ts`. Why: an evaluation can then find the turn's user message in the transcript with the same count, and cut right before it.
- **A version saved again for the same session and turn replaces the first.** That happens when a turn fails before its message reaches the transcript, so the next turn gets the same number. Why: the transcript holds only the second message, so the second version is the one that matches it.
- **A version is keyed by the session's `id`,** with a foreign key to `sessions`. The trip is found through the session. Why: the issue asks for the session and turn as the key, and the trip ID would be a second copy.
- **The app has a writer and no reader for versions.** That makes it nine classes that are the only way in, not eight (section 8). Why: only evaluation tooling reads versions. Its reader belongs with that tooling.
- **A migration that changes a plan document, a place row, or a memory item row has to change the versions' copies the same way.** Why: an evaluation runs a turn on today's code, so an old version has to load the way a trip row loads today. Example: the migration that dropped the trip brief's `restDaysText` would have had to remove it from each version too.
- **A failed version save fails the turn.** `CoordinatorTurns.begin()` throws, as it does when reading the trip fails. Not written into a design doc. Why: the save only fails when the database does, and then the turn would fail anyway.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes

None.

title: Save a trip version at the start of each turn

body:
## Task

Two changes from the review of #246 (trip versions):

- Say in the migrations paragraph (persistence design, section 1) that a migration that changes a plan document, a place row, or a memory item row changes the trip versions' copies the same way, so the rule is where migration authors look.
- Save each turn's user message in its trip version, and check it where an evaluation finds the turn in the transcript. A version's turn is found by counting user messages with the chat view's rule, so a later change to that rule could pair a version with the wrong moment. The check catches that.

## Results

- **The migrations paragraph:** done. Persistence design section 1 now states the rule and points to section 8.9.
- **The message is saved:** done. `CoordinatorTurns` passes the user's own words, and `TripVersionRepository.saveFrom()` writes them to the new `user_message` column (migration 0012). The turn test checks each of three versions holds its turn's message.
- **The check:** done. `turnMessageIndex()` in `src/agent/shown-messages.ts` finds turn N's message by the same count as `userMessageCount()`, and throws when the message there doesn't end with the one the version saved, when the transcript has no turn N, or when the version has no message. Tests cover each case.
- **Checked by hand against the local Postgres:** `npm run migrate` ran migration 0012. `saveFrom()` saved a version for a local session, with its plan and 21 places, and saving the same turn again replaced the message. The test row was removed afterward.
- **`npm run check`:** passes, 927 tests.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

All are written into the persistence design, section 8.9, unless noted.

- **The check is in the app's code now, not left to #245.** `turnMessageIndex()` sits next to `userMessageCount()`, so the count and the check share one rule (`userMessageLinesOf()`). #245's run tool uses it to find where to cut or fork the transcript.
- **The message must end with the saved words, not equal them after the app's lines are removed.** #245 rewords the app's date line. Old messages keep the old wording, which today's `withoutAppLines()` may not strip. Checking the end of the message works with any app lines in front of the user's words.
- **The version saves the user's own words, not the message with the app's lines.** The app's lines are built after the version is saved, and the user's words are what identifies the turn.
- **Versions saved before this get an empty message,** and the check refuses them. They're the few saved since #246 merged.
- **No separate check that a restored version matches today's schema.** The review of #246 suggested having #245 parse each restored plan with today's Zod schema. It isn't needed: the plan schema is strict (migration 0010's comment), so a version that a migration missed fails loudly the first time the coordinator reads the trip. Not written into a design doc.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes

None.

title: Keep each trip version's user message, and point migrations at the versions

body:
## Do

- Write the rebuild, and run it on the Bar Harbor session in the local database.
- Fix the rebuild until every checkpoint matches, or each difference left is listed in the PR with its reason.
- Write the versions to the live database.

## Done when

- The live database has a version for each turn of the session.
- Every checkpoint matches, apart from the differences listed in the PR.
- The rebuilt trip after the last turn matches the live trip, apart from the differences listed in the PR.
- `turnMessageIndex()` finds every version's turn in the live session's transcript, with no error.
- `npm run check` passes.

Closes #244

## Results

- **A version for each turn: done.** The session has 23 turns, and the live database now has 23 versions for it, turns 1 to 23. None has an empty message. The live rows are the same as the local ones: the md5 of all 23 rows matches.
- **Checkpoints: 18 of 19 match.** The 19 are 9 `read_itinerary`, 8 `read_worker_brief_facts`, 1 `read_trip_brief`, and 1 `read_memory`. The one difference:
  - Turn 1, `read_trip_brief`. The recorded reply says `comfortableDrivingInHours: not set`, and has a `restDaysText` line. Today's says `comfortableDrivingInHours: 4`, with no `restDaysText`. It can't match: since #230, a brief always holds comfortable driving hours, and `restDaysText` is gone. 4 is the value migration 0010 gave every brief with none.
- **The rebuilt trip against the live trip after the last turn: matches, apart from one difference.** Places (170) and memory (10 items) match exactly. The plan matches apart from `lastUpdatedDateTime`, which is 0.113 seconds earlier than the live one. The rebuild runs each call at the time it was made, and the live save came a moment later, during the call.
- **`turnMessageIndex()`: done.** After the write, the rebuild read the 23 versions back from the live database, and `turnMessageIndex()` found each one's turn in the live transcript, with no error.
- **`npm run check`: passes.**

### Calls rewritten into today's shape

None. Today's tools took all 88 recorded save calls as they were, and refused none.

### Other differences in the report

These aren't checkpoints, but the report lists them, for tracing:

- **15 write replies in turn 4,** from `add_stay`, `add_stops`, and `select_user_place`, name a daily driving warning the recorded replies didn't, such as "Day 1 needs about 5 h 29 m of driving." Before #230, a brief with no comfortable driving hours ran no daily driving check. Today's code checks against 4 hours. So the rebuild drops that check's results after each write, until the turn 5 `update_trip_brief` call that set comfortable driving to 6 hours. The stored trip, and so each version, holds the check results the coordinator saw.

### Checked by hand

- The rebuild against the local database, three times. The last run, from an empty local trip, is the one that wrote the versions to the live database.
- The local versions: each turn's saved time, its message, and how many places, memory items, and stays it holds, grow turn by turn as the transcript shows.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

The rebuild's general rules are written in persistence design section 8.9. The command is in DEVELOPMENT.md section 2.

- **Legs are routed by Google again,** as today's code does in each write's finish. The issue settled only that places aren't looked up again. Routing again keeps the replay going through today's code, with nothing stubbed. Every drive time in the 19 checkpoints matched the recorded ones.
- **Calls are put in the order they reached the trip:** a read by when it was called, and a change by when it was answered. Workers ran in parallel, so this is what makes a read see the writes that came before it.
- **A call refused when it was made is left out,** since it saved nothing. There were 4, all `add_stop_candidates` calls whose input the old schema refused.
- **A memory item keeps its live row's created time.** Today's `MemoryWriter` stamps the time it runs. The live time keeps memory in the order the coordinator read it.
- **Claude's choices go in a file outside the repo,** since they name places and calls from the session. The rebuild takes it with `--choices`. For this session it holds two things:
  - **4 live places that no reply names.** `search_along_leg` saves every place it finds, but leaves out of its reply any within 2 miles of either end of the drive, here Portland. These 4 are Portland seafood places, so they're added with the turn 5 lobster searches along Day 3 and Day 4. Every search they could have come from ran in turn 5, so the versions are the same whichever one it was.
  - **The daily driving check didn't run until turn 5.** Before #230, a brief with no comfortable driving hours ran no daily driving check. Its results are dropped after each write until the call that set them, so the versions hold the check results the coordinator saw. The issue's decision "What the coordinator saw wins over today's code" names this case.
- **The rebuild stops at a "forgot memory items" app line** rather than guess which item went, since the line doesn't say. This session has none. Handling it would be code no run uses.
- **Only a session that's its trip's only one can be rebuilt,** since the rebuild starts from an empty trip.
- **`read_worker_brief_facts` replies are checkpoints too,** besides the three the issue names. They show the brief at 8 later points, where `read_trip_brief` was read only once, in turn 1. All 8 match.
- **`newId()` can be handed the recorded IDs,** with `chooseNewIdsWith()` in `src/ids/new-id.ts`. Only the rebuild sets it, and it's cleared after each call. The trip and memory servers now export their tool lists (`tripTools()`, `memoryTools()`), so the rebuild calls the same tools the coordinator and workers get.
- **The live login comes from `LIVE_POSTGRES_*` variables,** filled in from the server's `.env` over SSH when the rebuild runs. Nothing is saved on this machine.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes

None needed.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)**

The replay's memory tools come from `memoryAccessFor({ pool, settings })`. That builds a `MemoryWriter` with the app's `tripStartedCheck`, and that check reads the system clock (`() => new Date()` in `src/persistence/trip-started-check.ts`). It doesn't read the replay clock. Every other write in the rebuild runs at `clock.at`: the `TripWriter` clock and the trip tools' `now`. So whether a trip memory item can be added, updated, or forgotten depends on the day the rebuild runs, not the time of the recorded call. Example: rerun the rebuild after the trip's start date. Every trip memory `add_memory_item`, `update_memory_item`, and `forget_memory_item` call is then refused as "trip has started". The rebuilt versions are missing those items. They show up only as "refused" entries in the report. A fix is to give the memory writer `tripStartedCheckUsing(..., () => clock.at)`.

**Why NF2:** The PR's run refused none of the 88 save calls, so the trip hadn't started when it ran. The bug only shows if this one-time job is rerun after the trip's start date, which is outside normal use. That rules out F2, so the label is NF2.

**Note (NF4 - Data is lost or corrupted, but not in normal use)**

`startLocalTrip` seeds the local trip with each user memory item created before turn 1. It copies the item's live row as it is now (`item.whole`), not as it was when the session started. Say a user memory item from before the session was updated later, by an `update_memory_item` call in this session or in a later session. Then the versions for the turns before that update hold the later text. The same goes for an item that existed at the start and was later forgotten. It has no live row, so it's missing from the early versions, and the replayed `forget_memory_item` fails. When the update happens in this session, the replayed update writes the same text. Its reply then matches the recorded one, so only a `read_memory` checkpoint taken before the update would show the wrong text.

**Why NF4:** This would corrupt the saved versions. But the PR says the session's one `read_memory` checkpoint matched and no call was refused, so it didn't happen in this run. The only remaining way is an update made after that read, which is unlikely in normal use, so the label is NF4 rather than F4.

title: Rebuild the Bar Harbor session's trip versions

body:
Closes #245

## Do

- Check first that the SDK resumes cleanly from copied lines. If the lines name the old agent session ID, or the copy needs anything else rewritten, rewrite it in the copy.
- Check whether the copied transcript names the old trip, session, or user ID anywhere the coordinator or its tools would use it. Rewrite any that would break the run.
- Change the app's date line, and add the rule to plan by it, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Update `withoutAppLines()` in `src/agent/app-lines.ts` to strip the new date line, and keep it stripping the old one. Live sessions recorded before this change keep the old wording, and the chat view still has to hide it. Add a test for each wording.
- Write the command, outside `npm run check`.
- Write how to use it into DEVELOPMENT.md section 5.

## Done when

- A run that starts the Bar Harbor session at turn 5, with the recorded message, gives the coordinator the same trip it saw in the recorded turn 5: its first read in the turn matches the recorded one, apart from format. The coordinator answers, and the turn's trace is in Phoenix.
- The same works with a new message.
- Nothing in the run tells the coordinator it isn't the recorded session. Check the run's transcript: after the copied lines, it has nothing the recorded turn didn't have, such as a resume line, apart from the turn itself and Claude Code's date change line. If needed, check a model call's full input with a logging proxy, as #188 did.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Results

- **Turn 5, recorded message: done, with the trip checked another way.** The run's first 199 transcript lines are the recorded ones, apart from the agent session ID. The run saves its own trip version at the start of the turn, as the app does. Its plan, places (10), memory (3), and message are the same as the recorded turn 5's version. Its saved time is 55 ms later, since the run's clock starts at the recorded turn's time and runs on. The coordinator answered, with 63 tool calls, and the turn's trace is in Phoenix (`road-trip-agent-local`, 102 spans). The first read can't be compared as the check says. Both turns made writes before their first read, and the writes differed, so the reads show different moments. In an earlier run, the first call was the same write as the recorded one, `update_trip_brief` with the same input, and its reply was the same.
- **Turn 5, new message: done.** Same version check, apart from the message. The coordinator answered, with 8 tool calls, and the trace is in Phoenix (17 spans). It ran at the same time as the recorded-message run, so two copies of the trip were in the local database at once.
- **Nothing tells the coordinator it's a run: done, with one more accepted difference.** After the copied lines, the turn's message is the recorded one, with no resumed line. Claude Code adds its date change line, as expected. It also adds an environment line, with the local working folder, git repository, shell, and OS version, since they differ from the server's. No thinking block was dropped. No logging proxy was needed, since Claude Code records what it adds, with the text it sends.
- **Turn 6, recorded message, as an extra check:** its copy holds the 5 worker transcripts from turn 5, and the first 453 lines match the recorded ones. The coordinator's reply builds on what those workers found.
- **The two checks in Do:** the SDK resumes cleanly from the copied lines, once each line's `sessionId` is the run's agent session ID. The recorded lines never name the trip's, session's, or user's own IDs. The agent session ID appears only in `sessionId`.
- **`npm run check`: passes.** 945 tests.

## Checked by hand

- Migration 0013 ran on the local database. The keys are `(trip_id, id)` for places and `(user_id, id)` for memory items.
- A two-turn local chat, then a run of its turn 2 through the command, with the source pointed at the local database. Its transcript after the copied lines matches the recorded turn.
- Which change drops the coordinator's earlier thinking, on that local session: a changed system prompt dropped none, and a changed date line in the first message dropped all 6 blocks after it.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **Copied lines stay exactly as recorded. This changes a decision in the issue.** The issue said the copy rewrites each old date line into the new wording. But the API ties each of the coordinator's thinking blocks to the conversation before it, and drops the block when that has changed. In the first turn 5 run, the rewrite of the first message's date line dropped all 17 earlier thinking blocks. On a local session, a changed date line dropped every block after it, and a changed system prompt dropped none. So the copy changes only the agent session ID, which isn't sent to the model. The instructions now name the old wording as the same line, which a live session started before this change also needs once it's resumed. Written into persistence design 8.9 and technical spec 5.2.
- **The date line wording, for your review:** "For planning this trip, today's date is Sunday, October 10, 2027." The rule added to the instructions: "Earlier messages may give it in an older wording, "Today is" and the date, such as "Today is Sunday, October 10, 2027." It's the same line. Plan by this date. Every rule that uses today's date, such as the earliest start date, whether a stay is close enough for a forecast, or whether the trip has started, goes by the date in the last of these lines, even when another date shows up." The diff is in `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`.
- **Claude Code's environment line is a second accepted difference.** On resume, Claude Code says the working folder, git repository, shell, and OS version changed, since they're the laptop's, not the server's. Matching them would mean running the turn on the server. Written into persistence design 8.9, next to the date change line.
- **Places are keyed by trip and ID, and memory items by user and ID.** Decided by you in chat. Migration 0013. `PlaceRepository.fillNames()` now takes the trip. The rebuild's three queries that found a row by ID alone now name the user or the trip too, so they can't touch a run's copies. Written into persistence design section 2.
- **The SDK's queue markers for the turn's message are left out of the copy.** They come just before the message, and the run's own message gets its own pair, so keeping them doubled them. The model never sees them. Persistence design 8.9.
- **The app's clock in a run starts at the version's saved time and runs on from there,** rather than stopping at it, so times saved during the turn keep their order. Each access function now takes a required `now`, and the memory tools' started-trip check uses it too. The app and the terminal chat pass the system clock.
- **The command takes exactly one of `--recorded-message` or `--message "<text>"`,** so a run never picks the message silently. It's `npm run run-turn`.
- **A run saves its own trip version at the start of its turn,** since it goes through `CoordinatorTurns` like any turn. That's what the Done when check compared.
- **The live database login code moved to `src/config/live-env.schema.ts`,** so the rebuild and the run share it.

## Set aside

- Two things for the evaluations: start each one-turn evaluation with `npm run run-turn` and leave the copied lines alone, and watch whether the coordinator reacts to the two accepted lines. Both added to the Do of #53.

## Config changes

None needed.

Line 266.

**Note (N6 - A design doc is unclear, or doesn't match the code, in a way no builder would act on)**

The class diagram in persistence design section 8.1 still shows `fillNames(places : List~Place~)`. This PR changed `PlaceRepository.fillNames()` to take `(tripId, places)`, and section 8.7 at line 445 now says `fillNames(tripId, places)`. So the diagram and the text in the same doc no longer agree on the signature.

**Why N6:** The doc doesn't match the code. Section 8.7 and the code both give the new signature, so no builder would act on the stale diagram line. That makes it N6, not F6.

title: Start a run from any turn of a recorded session
ignore phoenix-tutorials

body:
## Do

Add each of these to the coordinator's instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and the files next to it), in the section it fits:

- **"What's left to decide?"** How to answer it, from technical spec 5.2: a whole read and trip memory, then the stops and lodging still empty or proposed, the open warnings, and the open items in trip memory. Mention approved exceptions briefly. Nothing in the instructions covers it today.
- **The contiguous United States only.** The app plans trips only there, as functional spec sections 1 and 2 say. Don't offer, or add, a stay or stop outside it, such as Niagara Falls, Ontario.
- **Replies are for the user.** Don't write notes to yourself as reply text, such as "I need to read brief and memory first."
- **A standing preference also goes to user memory,** even when the trip brief holds it for this trip. Technical spec 5.2, "Writing memory", has the rule and its example: "we never drive more than 5 hours, on any trip" sets comfortable driving hours, and is saved to user memory too. Today the Memory section has only the trip memory half of the rule: don't save to trip memory what the trip brief or the itinerary holds.
- **Stops the user chose decide their own part of the road.** If they're inland, the leg runs inland there, and the coordinator doesn't question it (technical spec 4.2, "The route preference is for the stretches nobody has decided"). The instructions cover only the waypoints half.
- **A stop whose purpose says how long:** when telling the user what it pushes later in the day, use the same rough timing as the worker brief (technical spec 5.2). Today the instructions don't tie the two together, so they could differ.

Also:

- Fix technical spec 4.2's step 4, "Fill". It says a stay researcher goes to a stay with "lodging not yet selected". Section 5.2, and the instructions, send one only for lodging with no candidates yet. 5.2 is right: lodging that already has candidates doesn't need another researcher. Change 4.2 to match.
- The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, so the coordinator's view file shows the changes.

## Done when

- The PR description lists each item in "Do", with the part of the instructions that now covers it.
- `npm run check` passes.

Closes #65

## Results

**Each item in "Do", with the part of the instructions that now covers it:**

- **"What's left to decide?"**: a new last bullet in "Reading the trip brief, the itinerary, and memory".
- **The contiguous United States only**: a new bullet in "Conduct".
- **Replies are for the user**: a new bullet in "Conduct".
- **A standing preference also goes to user memory**: a new bullet in "Memory", under "Writing memory", right after the trip memory rule it qualifies.
- **Stops the user chose decide their own part of the road**: a new last bullet in "How to plan a trip", right after the scenic waypoints bullet.
- **A stop whose purpose says how long**: two more sentences on the bullet in "Laying out days", and one on the "When:" bullet in "Worker briefs", so each points to the other.
- **Technical spec 4.2, step 4**: now says lodging with no candidates yet, and why lodging with candidates needs no researcher.
- **`npm run agent-views`**: run. `src/agent/coordinator.view.md` shows each change.

**`npm run check`:** passes. 129 test files, 945 tests.

Nothing was checked by hand. The change is wording only, and its effect on the agent is for the evaluations in #53 and #69 to show.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

Joe agrees to these by approving the PR.

1. **The contiguous US rule goes in "Conduct", and also in technical spec 5.2's Conduct bullet.** It applies to every round, from the sketches to a single stop, so no one planning section fits it. The issue noted that 5.2 didn't say it, so a check of the instructions against 5.2 alone would miss it. Writing it into 5.2 closes that gap. The rule also covers the start and end place, not only stays and stops, since a trip that starts in Toronto leaves the contiguous US just as much. When the user asks for a place outside it, the coordinator says so and offers the US side where there is one, such as Niagara Falls, New York, rather than just refusing.

2. **"Replies are for the user" goes in "Conduct", and in technical spec 5.2.** It's about how the coordinator talks, like the other Conduct rules. The wording says why: text before a tool call is shown to the user. Telling the model where its planning belongs ("Plan in your thinking") gives it somewhere to put the note, rather than only a ban. The coordinator has thinking on (technical spec 5.4).

3. **"What's left to decide?" says to read the itinerary and trip memory again**, even mid-session. Another session may have changed the trip, and a fresh whole read is short. It says "nothing selected, saying which have options to pick from and which have none yet" instead of "empty or proposed". The prompt never defines those two words, and the user cares about the difference: one needs a pick from a card, the other needs a worker. Approved warnings are mentioned so the user knows they're settled, which is why 5.2 asks for them. No design doc change: 5.2 already has the rule.

4. **The stop-duration timing is tied both ways.** The "Laying out days" bullet says to work out the times as for "When:" in a worker brief, with an example (a 5-hour Arches hike from 8:30 puts lunch around 2:00, in the reply and the worker brief). The "When:" bullet says to use the same times told to the user. The two are written at different moments, often turns apart, so each place needs the reminder. The heading comes from `WORKER_BRIEF_HEADING`, so it can't drift.

5. **The inland-stops rule names no real place.** The example is "a winery they picked on a coast trip." A real inland town would need checking against which roads actually run there, and a wrong example would teach the wrong road.

6. **Technical spec 4.2's step 4 says why** lodging with candidates gets no researcher: the user picks from its card. That keeps the reason next to the rule.

## Set aside

- **A leg between two US places can route through Canada,** such as Detroit to Buffalo on Ontario's Highway 401. No tool shows the road a route takes, so the new rule can't catch it. Opened #253 in Triage, with two ways to handle it and the question of whether it's worth it.

## Config changes

None.

## Decisions

1. **A gone warning reads `- Fixed by this change: the earlier warning that said "<saved text>"`.** It's the tested line's start, and code can produce it from the saved text alone. "That said" puts the quoted text in the past, so it reads as what was true before the change. Written into tool design 2.1.
2. **A gone note reads `- Cleared by this change: the earlier note that said "<saved text>"`.** A note isn't a problem, such as a faster stop order, so "fixed" would be wrong for it. This wording wasn't tested with the judges, since turn 10 has only a warning. Written into tool design 2.1 and technical spec 5.2.
3. **A warning that went away because its stop or stay was removed also reads "Fixed".** One word per level keeps the code simple, and the warning is no longer a problem either way.
4. **A reply with nothing to list reads "No check results are new or changed, and this change fixed or cleared none."** It uses the same words as the lines, and drops "gone". Written into tool design 2.1.
5. **The saved text's caveats stay in the quote,** such as "this time may be too early". Code can't strip them reliably, and the turn 10 test passed with them in.
6. **The coordinator's instructions changed in two places:** the rule on what a write's reply lists, and the Big Sur example in "Check results", which said "the warning is gone". It now says "that change fixes the warning". No tool description mentions gone results. I didn't add a new rule about fixed results, since the line itself says the change fixed it, and "Every other warning is open until a change makes it go away" already covers it. Technical spec 5.2 has the same two changes.
7. **`day-tools.test.ts`'s scenic approval test now checks the whole reply.** It checked that the reply had no "cleared", to show no waypoints were cleared. The new no-results line has that word, so the test now asserts the exact reply, as the fastest approval test next to it does.

## Turn 10 test

One wording tried, the line this code prints for the Twelve warning:

`- Fixed by this change: the earlier warning that said "Twelve is closed for the whole visit, on Saturday, May 22, 2027. You'd get there at 10:47 a.m., with 1 h planned. Times are estimates from average drive times. An earlier stop on this day has no place picked yet, so this time may be too early."`

Nothing.

None needed.

**Note (N3 - Text a road trip agent reads is unclear, or says something twice, or is an error message with the wrong reason for a failure)**

The coordinator's check results instructions now use "cleared" for two different things. A write's reply says "Cleared by this change: the earlier note that said ..." when a note went away. The same section still says "The write that clears the mark returns the warning as new", where "clears" means the "may be too early" mark came off a warning that's still open. A coordinator that links the two could read "cleared" as "went away" in the opening-hours rule, or expect a "Cleared by this change" line when a mark comes off. Saying "The write that removes the mark" would keep "cleared" for results that went away.

**Why N3:** This is text the coordinator reads that's unclear, not false. Both sentences are true on their own, so it isn't F3. The code and docs match the task, so no D or F label fits.

## Do

- Add `npm run live-chat`, in TypeScript under `src/`, next to `src/chat.ts`. It talks to the app only through its API, never the database or the coordinator. Reuse what's in `src/shared/`, such as `messageRequestSchema`, `chatEventSchema` and `src/shared/chat-event-parser.ts`, and `src/shared/itinerary.schema.ts`, so `npm run check` catches the client breaking when the API changes.
- Run one command per action, and exit when it's done. A simulated user's harness runs one shell command at a time, so a long-running prompt like `npm run chat`'s won't work. It has to:
  - start a trip with a first message (`POST /api/trips`), and print the new trip and session IDs.
  - send a message to a session (`POST /api/sessions/:sessionId/messages`).
  - start a new session on a trip (`POST /api/trips/:tripId/sessions`), and open an old session (`POST /api/sessions/:sessionId/resume`), as a user does who comes back another day.
  - print the itinerary, as the itinerary view shows it.
  - print the open option cards, with a number on each option.
  - send a card's buttons: Select on an option, More options, Higher tier, and Lower tier. Send the same message and the same option card IDs a click sends (`web/src/option-card.tsx`). Move the words of those messages into `src/shared/`, so the web page and the client can't drift apart.
- Read the message from standard input, so it can be more than one line, and needs no shell quoting.
- Print only what the web page shows: the reply text, and while a turn runs, the name of each tool the coordinator calls, as the chat's "waiting on" line shows it. Never the thinking, the tool inputs, or the tool replies. After each reply, say how many option cards are open, so the simulated user knows to look, as a web user sees a card appear.
- Sign in with Supabase's email and password sign-in, as `web/src/sign-in-page.tsx` does. The site's address, the email, and the password come from environment values, checked with Zod when the command starts. Never take the password as a command-line argument, since a harness shows each command it runs. The Supabase URL and publishable key are already in `.env` as `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
- The site's address can be the local stack, `http://localhost:5173` with `npm run dev`, or the live site, `https://roadtrip.jjk3.com`. Both use the same Supabase project, so the same user signs in to either (systems design, section 6).
- Add a `whoami` action that signs in and prints the user's ID and email, from Supabase's sign-in reply. #66 uses it to list each bot user's ID with its harness and model, with no Supabase admin key.
- Add the command to DEVELOPMENT.md section 2.
- A turn can take minutes when workers run. The longest in Phoenix so far took about 4 minutes. Wait for the turn's end event, with no timeout of the client's own.

## Done when

- Against the local stack, with a Supabase user made for testing: a short chat starts a trip, gets an option card, selects an option with the client, and asks for a higher tier with it. Each turn's trace is in the `road-trip-agent-local` Phoenix project, under that user's ID.
- The client's output for those turns shows only reply text, tool names, and the card count.
- No check runs against the live site. Its first real use is #67.

Closes #251

## Results

- **A short chat against the local stack, with a Supabase user made for testing: done.** Claude's own user (`SUPABASE_CLAUDE_EMAIL`, user ID `145b1f61-a9e8-4824-b48f-6a50c9c58659`), with `npm run dev`. `start` made trip `trip_qgxrm22q` and got a lodging card for Moab. `higher` on that card got three nicer places, and `select` picked one of them. Then `open`, `send`, and `new-session` each ran once. All five turns' `coordinator.turn` spans are in the `road-trip-agent-local` Phoenix project, with `user.id` set to that user's ID. The two card turns' inputs start with the app's line, "From an option card: stay_dcqnky3x." and "From an option card: stay_dcqnky3x, place_yp5n9had.", so the IDs went the way a click sends them.
- **The client's output shows only reply text, tool names, and the card count: done.** Each turn printed a "Working: <tool>…" line per tool call, the reply, and the count. A click's message is printed too, as the user's message, since the chat shows it as one. No thinking, tool inputs, or tool replies. Sample below.
- **No check ran against the live site.**
- `npm run check` passes. A new test (`src/live-chat/live-chat-actions.test.ts`) covers what's printed for a turn, how a card and option number turn into the IDs and words a click sends, a tier button the card doesn't show, and a turn that fails.

Checked by hand: `whoami` printed the user's ID and email. `select` with a card or option number that doesn't exist was refused with the numbers that do. `itinerary` printed the plan, with "option card 1 is open" in the lodging's place. `npm run build:web` still builds. ## Decisions

The client is a dev tool, so these went into DEVELOPMENT.md section 2 and the comment at the top of `src/live-chat/live-chat.ts`, not a design doc.

- **Every action after the first message takes the session ID.** `itinerary` and `cards` look up the session's trip with `GET /api/sessions/:sessionId`, which doesn't count as a resume. Only `new-session` takes a trip ID, since there's no session yet. A simulated user then keeps track of one ID, not two.
- **Cards are numbered in the order the itinerary view shows them,** each stay's lodging first, then each day's stops. Options are numbered within their card, so Select is `select <session ID> <card> <option>`. Each command reads the itinerary again, so the numbers match what the last `cards` printed, as long as no turn changed the plan in between.
- **A tier button the card doesn't show is refused,** such as `higher` on a card whose options are already the nicest. The page hides that button, so a web user couldn't click it either.
- **A click's message is printed as the user's message,** such as `> Select Sunflower Hill Inn for the lodging in Moab.` The chat shows it that way.
- **`itinerary` shows "option card 2 is open" where the page shows the card itself.** `cards` prints the cards. This keeps the itinerary short enough to read in one go.
- **A selected place's "why" is printed under it.** On the page it's one click away. A simulated user can't click, so the text is printed.
- **The client's environment values are `LIVE_CHAT_SITE`, `LIVE_CHAT_EMAIL`, and `LIVE_CHAT_PASSWORD`.** The Supabase address and key come from the web page's own `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`. The command loads `.env` for those, as the other npm commands do. Values set in the shell win over `.env`, so a harness can set each bot user's own. A bad value is named, never printed.
- **A message's reply is read with Node's `http` module, not `fetch`.** Node's `fetch` gives up on a reply after 5 minutes with no data. A turn can be quiet that long while a worker runs. The issue says to wait with no timeout of the client's own.
- **`open` waits while a turn is still running,** and asks again every 5 seconds, as the browser does. Then it prints the conversation so far and the card count.
- **A failed turn, or a stream that closes before the turn's end, exits with status 1,** after the same kind of notice the page shows. A harness can then tell the turn didn't finish.
- **Shared text moved to `src/shared/`:** the option card's message words and how a message names the stop or stay (`option-card-text.ts`), the card's facts text, `dates.ts`, `itinerary-text.ts` with the stop kinds' names, and the short tool name (`tool-name.ts`). The web page and the client then show and send the same words.
- **The client is in its own folder, `src/live-chat/`,** as `npm run run-turn` is in `src/turn-run/`. It's six files, not one.

## Set aside

Nothing.

## Config changes

None needed.

<!-- fix-loop: summary -->

## Fix loop: deferred, and needs attention

Code updates this comment after each fix round. Resolve a finding's thread once it's handled. A finding in a review body has no thread, so tick its box instead.

**Deferred**

None.

**Needs attention**

None.

**Fix (F2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, in normal use)**

When a reply's stream is cut off partway through a turn, the client crashes with a raw stack trace. It never prints its own message for that case. `HttpSiteApi.send()` reads the response with `for await (const chunk of chunks)`. When the server or a proxy drops the socket before the final chunk, Node's `IncomingMessage` throws `Error: aborted` with code `ECONNRESET`; it doesn't end cleanly. I checked this with a local HTTP server that sends one `toolCall` event and then destroys the socket: the loop threw `ECONNRESET aborted`. That error isn't a `LiveChatError`, so the `catch` at the bottom of `live-chat.ts` throws it again, and the process dies with a stack trace. So `printTurn()` never prints "The connection closed before the reply finished. Open the session again to see the rest." That message only shows when the stream ends cleanly with no `ended` event, which a dropped connection doesn't do. A concrete case: a 4-minute turn on the live site, cut off by a restart or a network blip. The simulated user's harness gets a Node stack trace instead of the hint to run `open`, while the browser shows its CUT_OFF message in the same case. The same thing happens when `fetch` in `#json` fails, such as `TypeError: fetch failed` when `npm run dev` isn't running. One fix is to catch the stream's error in `send()` or `printTurn()` and treat it as the cut-off case.

**Why F2:** A dropped connection during a long turn is a failure the code is meant to handle, since `printTurn()` has a branch and a message for it, so this is normal use. The client crashes instead of printing that message. The task is still done and no agent-facing text is false, so F1 and F3 don't fit, and no D label fits because the claim checked out when I ran it.

**Fixed** in 9369d23f870aa6a72a9019d418b6c1989ec70d6f.

`HttpSiteApi.send()` now reads the reply through `chunksUntilClosed()`. A read error, such as `Error: aborted` from a dropped socket, ends those chunks the same way a clean close does. So `printTurn()` prints "The connection closed before the reply finished. Open the session again to see the rest.", and the command exits with status 1. Only the socket read is caught. A bad event from `ChatEventParser` still throws. A connection that fails before any reply, from `fetch` in `#json` or the request in `#postForStream`, now throws a `LiveChatError` ("Couldn't reach <site>: <reason>") through `#unreachable()`. Before the fix, the new tests in `src/live-chat/site-api.test.ts` failed with `Error: aborted` and `fetch failed`. One test runs `startTrip` against a local server that sends a session event and a toolCall, then destroys the socket. The other sends to a port nothing listens on.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)**

`HttpSiteApi.#json()` runs `JSON.parse(text)` on any 200 reply without catching the error. A 200 reply that isn't JSON makes the command crash with a raw `SyntaxError` stack trace, not a `LiveChatError` message. An example is `LIVE_CHAT_SITE` set to a host that serves the web page's `index.html` for unknown paths, with no `/api` proxy in front. Then `npm run live-chat -- cards <session ID>` prints `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'` and a stack trace. The error-status branch handles non-JSON with `errorMessageOf()`, but the success branch doesn't. One fix is to wrap the parse and throw a `LiveChatError` that says the site's reply wasn't the API's JSON.

**Why NF2:** It happens only when the site address points at something that isn't the app's API. That's a misconfiguration, not a trip or a failure the code is meant to handle, so it's NF2 and not F2. The claim holds as the code stands, so D1 doesn't fit, and no design doc speaks to it, so D2 doesn't fit.

Create a small PR that sets what files ESLint should read versus what it should ignore, so a gitignored folder can't break `npm run check`.

## Result

nodes.body:
**Decisions**

- **The list lives in the lint command, not in `eslint.config.mjs`.** ESLint then never opens a folder that isn't named, so a new gitignored folder can't fail the check. Prettier already works this way, with `prettier --check src web`.
- **The ignore list in `eslint.config.mjs` stays as it is.** The per-edit hook (`.claude/hooks/check-edited-file.sh`) passes a single file to ESLint, and the lint command's list doesn't apply there. Without the ignore list, editing a file in `scratch/` would fail that hook.
- **A new top-level code folder or config file won't be linted until it's added to the command.** That's accepted, since all the code lives in `src/` and `web/`.

**Set aside:** nothing.

**Config changes:** none. `package.json` isn't one of the files in DEVELOPMENT.md section 6.

body:
## Do

- Make a `simulated-users/` folder in the repo. It holds:
  - `instructions.md`, what every simulated user gets.
  - `trips/`, one trip file per trip.
  - `personas/`, one persona file per persona.
  - `bot-users.md`, each bot user's ID with its email.
  - `README.md`, how to add a bot user, set up a run, and start each harness. Joe refers to it, so it has to work on its own.
- A trip file holds:
  - the facts the user knows, such as dates, places, budget, and driving limits.
  - things the user hasn't decided yet.
  - changes to make partway through, and when, such as skipping Denver once the first draft is done.
  - when the trip counts as planned, so the simulated user knows when to stop.

  The facts also work as an answer key, to check what the coordinator saved to the trip brief. A persona file holds only how the user talks and acts, with nothing about any one trip.
- Add a setup script that makes a run folder, such as `npm run sim-setup -- codex-gpt-5 moab curt`, for a bot user, a trip, and a persona. It also takes the site, local or live. The folder goes in `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/`, named for the three, such as `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/codex-gpt-5-moab-curt/`. It stops if that folder is already there, so an old run's files never mix with a new one. The folder gets:
  - `instructions.md`, and copies of the trip file and the persona file named plainly `trip.md` and `persona.md`, so nothing in the folder hints at other trips.
  - `account.env`, the bot user's email and password from `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/<bot user>.env`, plus `LIVE_CHAT_SITE` for the site. It uses the names `live-chat` already reads: `LIVE_CHAT_SITE`, `LIVE_CHAT_EMAIL`, and `LIVE_CHAT_PASSWORD`.
  - `chat.sh`, which loads `account.env` and runs `npm run live-chat` in the repo, passing its arguments and standard input through. Values set in the shell win over the repo's `.env`, so the bot user's values are the ones used.
- The instructions say how to use `./chat.sh`: starting the trip, sending messages, looking at the option cards and the itinerary, and using the card buttons. They also say how to act: answer only what's asked, give one or two facts at a time, and stick with any answer it makes up. A web user sees the cards and the itinerary beside the chat without asking, so the instructions say to look at them as a user would, such as after a reply says a card is open.
- Write down how to add a harness:
  - Joe makes one bot user per harness and model pair, in the Supabase dashboard (systems design, section 3). Its email and password go in `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/<bot user>.env`, outside the repo, so they can't be committed.
  - Keep a list in the repo of each bot user's ID with its email, starting with the bot user above, so a session in Phoenix can be traced to who played it. Phoenix shows only the user's ID. Each line comes from running `npm run live-chat`'s `whoami` as that bot user. No passwords in the list.
  - Each harness starts in the run folder, so it doesn't load the repo's `CLAUDE.md`. Joe's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` still loads for some harnesses, so the README gives each one's start command:
    - Claude Code: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude claude --model <model>`. Its own config folder keeps out Joe's `CLAUDE.md`, settings, and memory. Joe signs in once in that config folder.
    - Codex: `codex -m <model>`. It reads only `AGENTS.md`, and Joe has none.
    - opencode: `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1 opencode -m <model>`. opencode falls back to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when it has no `AGENTS.md` of its own.

    Every harness then gets the same opening prompt, such as "Read instructions.md, trip.md, and persona.md, then plan the trip."
  - Check the harness lets a shell command it waits on run at least 5 minutes, since a turn with workers can take about 4. Ask it to run `python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(330)'; echo done` in the foreground, without setting a timeout itself. If it doesn't print "done", raise the harness's command timeout in its settings, and try again. Don't use `sleep` for the check: Claude Code refuses a foreground `sleep`, and runs it in the background, where there's no limit to test. Claude Code cuts a command off after 2 minutes by default. Its config folder's `settings.json` raises that with `"env": { "BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000", "BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000" }`. Checked on 2026-11-04 with Claude Code 2.1.318.
- Write the San Francisco trip file, from domain model section 5.1, with changes partway through, and one persona file. The trip is planned in one session. A change may start a new session right away, but never on a later day, so leave out changes such as the user opening the trip again on May 8, 2027. Joe decided on 2026-11-04, in chat, that coming back to a trip later isn't tested here. The San Francisco changes in the design walkthroughs' last prompt (`reviews/walkthroughs/prompt-6.md`, section "Changes to make along the way") are a starting point. That prompt is out of date, so check each change still fits the current design.
- Run the whole San Francisco trip with Claude Code and Sonnet against the local stack (`npm run dev`), signed in as its bot user. The implementer starts it, headless, in the run folder: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude claude -p --model sonnet --allowedTools "Bash(./chat.sh:*)"`, in the background, and reads the session when it ends. Give the opening prompt on standard input, since `--allowedTools` takes a list and would read a prompt after it as one more tool. Allow more tools only if the run shows the simulated user needs them. Fix the problems it finds in the setup, the trip file, the persona file, or the instructions. File any app bug as a new issue. A fix that changes the design goes to Joe first.
- In DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, point to `simulated-users/README.md` for how to run a simulated user.

## Done when

- One harness plays the San Francisco trip from start to finish against the local stack, and stops when the trip file says the trip is planned.
- Each problem the run found is fixed, or filed as an issue.
- A new harness can be added, and a run set up and started, from `simulated-users/README.md`, with no other help.

Closes #66

## Results

- **One harness plays the San Francisco trip from start to finish against the local stack, and stops when the trip file says the trip is planned.** Done. Claude Code with Sonnet, headless, as the issue says, against `npm run dev`. The last run, with the final setup, planned the trip in 36 turns, 17 minutes, and $0.44 of the simulated user's own usage. It made all seven changes in the trip file, started a new session, asked what was left to decide, and stopped when the planner said nothing. No command was refused or failed. Trip `trip_jumkhgwb`, sessions `session_bp8rqry8` and `session_rsf8wtdp`, in the local database and in `road-trip-agent-local`.
- **Each problem the run found is fixed, or filed as an issue.** Three runs before the last one found these:
  - The simulated user piped `cards` into `sed`, and the permission rule refused it. It then ran the command alone. The instructions now say to run each command on its own.
  - It sent several clicks at once, by card number. The numbers shifted once a card closed, so one click hit a card that wasn't there, and one may have hit the wrong card. Fixed in code, so it doesn't depend on the model. `live-chat` now names each card by its stop's or stay's ID, which doesn't shift, and refuses a card that has closed. `chat.sh` refuses to start while another `chat.sh` command in the run is still going.
  - It never looked at the itinerary. The instructions now say when to: when the days are first laid out, and after each change. In the later runs, it looked two or three times a run.
  - No app bug came up. One thing about the app was filed: in every run, the planner added "the schedule shows that walk as a short drive" after most picks. #262, in Triage.
- **A new harness can be added, and a run set up and started, from `simulated-users/README.md`, with no other help.** The README covers adding a bot user, the bot user list, `npm run sim-setup`, each harness's start command, the headless start for Claude Code, and the command timeout check. Each run here was set up and started with only the README's commands.

## Checked by hand

- `npm run sim-setup` made the run folder, and stopped when it was already there. `./chat.sh whoami` in the folder signed in as `claude-code-sonnet@jjk3.com`, user ID `d37cc40c-3a8f-4ece-ba59-f1309c7b3e39`, the line in `bot-users.md`.
- Two `./chat.sh whoami` commands started together: the second was refused with the "still running" message, and one run alone afterward went through.

nodes.body:
## Decisions

- **Option cards are named by their stop's or stay's ID in `live-chat`, not by their place in the list.** Joe asked in chat to fix model mistakes in code where we can, since open-weight models will be harder to steer. A number shifts once an earlier card closes, so a click from an old list could hit the wrong card. An ID doesn't shift, and a closed card's ID is refused. Options are still numbered, since they change only when that card's own options do. Written in DEVELOPMENT.md section 2, `simulated-users/instructions.md`, and the comment in `src/live-chat/option-cards.ts`.
- **`chat.sh` refuses to start while another `chat.sh` command in the run is still going.** For the same reason: Sonnet sent several clicks at once in one run. It locks `chat.sh` itself with `flock`, which Linux has and macOS doesn't. Written in `simulated-users/README.md`.
- **When to look at the itinerary stays in the instructions, not in code.** Code could print the whole itinerary after each reply, but it's long, and real users don't always look either. Whether the simulated user looks is part of how it plays a user.
- **The setup script is TypeScript, in `src/sim-setup/`,** like the other dev commands, so it's linted and tested. It reads the account file with Node's `parseEnv` and checks it with Zod (DEVELOPMENT.md section 4). The bot user's name is its email before the `@`. `live` means `https://roadtrip.jjk3.com`.
- **The San Francisco trip file follows domain model 5.1,** with the changes from the old walkthrough prompt, checked against the current design:
  - Mike's address is a house number on a real Silver Lake street, so Google finds it as an address, not a business.
  - Hangar One stays, though it isn't open to the public. The planner caught that in each run, which is a good case for the "grounded in the record" evaluator (#53).
  - "Let's try the Sardine Factory after all" stays. The design says a rejection can't be taken back, so the user accepts that and keeps The Whaling Station.
  - The reopen on May 8, 2027 is left out, as the issue says. In its place, change 7 starts a new session right away and asks what's left to decide, as Moab's old step 7 did.
  - The simulated user stops after 80 messages if the trip still isn't planned, so a stuck run can't go on and on.
- **The one persona is `easygoing`:** short casual messages, goes along with suggestions, firm about places it named. It's the most common kind of user, so it's a good first baseline.
- **The headless start in the README adds `--output-format stream-json --verbose`,** written outside the run folder, so a run can be watched while it plays, and the simulated user can't read its own log.

## Set aside

- Short walks shown as drives in the schedule, which the planner explained again after most picks. Filed as #262, in Triage.

## Config changes

None. The new `sim-setup` script is in `package.json`, which isn't one of the config files in DEVELOPMENT.md section 6.

Line 203.

**Note (N1 - Cleaner code)**

`numberArg()` still says `"x" isn't a card or option number.`, but this PR makes cards go by ID. `numberArg` is now called only for the option number, in `select`. So `./chat.sh select session_1 stay_moab two` tells the simulated user that a card number is wrong, when cards no longer have numbers. The message should only say it isn't an option number.

**Why N1:** The text is out of date, but only a simulated user or a developer reads it. No road trip agent sees it, so this isn't N3 or F3. It's a small cleanup.

Line 615.

**Note (NF2 - The app does the wrong thing, crashes, or hangs, but not in normal use)**

`siteAddress()` looks the site up in `SITES`, which is a plain object literal typed as `Record<string, string>`. A site name that matches a key inherited from `Object.prototype`, such as `constructor` or `toString`, returns a function, not `undefined`, so the check passes. I ran `setUpRun` with `site: 'constructor'`, and it got past the site check. With real trip and persona files, it would then crash in `shellQuoted()` with a TypeError instead of printing `"constructor" isn't a site.` The fix is `Object.hasOwn(SITES, site)` or a `Map`.

**Why NF2:** The app does the wrong thing, but only for a site name nobody would type at `npm run sim-setup`. That puts it outside normal use.

Closes #67

## Results

**The session is in Phoenix.** One run, on 2026-11-04 from 19:59 to 20:12 UTC, about 13 minutes. Trip `trip_mfvyzu8x`, with two app sessions, `session_x684eqc8` and `session_3rberk77`. In the `road-trip-agent` project they're the Phoenix sessions `6a5a3840-2911-46d0-8579-aae28f06961b` (22 turns) and `aa5d567a-ce94-4333-8c68-9307e17c9b33` (2 turns). Every `coordinator.turn` span has `user.id` `d37cc40c-3a8f-4ece-ba59-f1309c7b3e39`, which is `claude-code-sonnet` in `bot-users.md`. The simulated user used 33 messages and about $0.42. **It stuck to the trip file: passed.** Every fact it gave matches the trip file. Where the trip file had no answer, it made up ones that fit: Sunday works for Mike, and a bit more for a Big Sur hotel is fine. All seven changes were made, in order, at the points the trip file says. The Sardine Factory couldn't come back, since a rejection can't be taken back (functional spec section 2), so it kept The Whaling Station, as the trip file says.

**It acted like a user: passed, with three small slips.**

- It held back one must-see. Asked for must-sees, it gave three, and brought up the Madonna Inn cake later, as a dessert stop.
- It tried a pipe once (`./chat.sh cards ... | sed ...`). The permission check refused it, and it ran `./chat.sh cards` alone.
- On "Take the second one," the planner took Garden Street Inn, the second hotel in its own list. The simulated user meant the second on the card, Petit Soleil. It said Garden Street "was the third one in your list," which was true of the card but not the list, and the planner switched. Its final note calls this the planner's mistake, but both readings are fine.

**The trip brief matches the trip file's facts: passed.** From the last `mcp__trip__read_trip_brief` span, at 20:12:10 UTC, on the new session's first turn:

| Trip file | Brief |
|---|---|
| Highway 1, San Francisco to Los Angeles | focus: California coast, San Francisco to Los Angeles |
| 3 days (went to 4 and back) | tripLengthInDays: 3 |
| coast views, aviation, good food | interestsText: coast views, seafood and tri-tip, old planes |
| Boardwalk, Bixby, elephant seals, Madonna Inn cake | mustSeesText: Boardwalk, Bixby, elephant seals |
| about 4 hours a day | comfortableDrivingInHours: 4 |
| scenic | routePreference: scenic |
| 8 a.m. | usualStartTime: 8:00 a.m. |
| local café breakfasts, casual lunches, nicer dinners | mealPreferencesText: the same |
| mid-range | lodgingPreferencesText: mid range hotels |

The cake isn't in `mustSeesText`, since the user didn't give it as a must-see, but it's a stop on Day 2. The rest is in the itinerary: May 13, 2027, San Francisco to Mike's place in Silver Lake, and the fastest route on Day 3.

**App bugs filed:** one, #265, `live-chat` printing a picked place's reason and source on one line. The run also showed the stay researcher's candidate calls refused 7 times. That's agent behavior, not an app bug, so it's in its own Triage issue, #266.

**Checked by hand:** the run's log, every message the simulated user sent, and the spans above, read from the `road-trip-agent` Phoenix project through the SSH tunnel. `npm run check` passes.
